eng_text: He said, "The Kingdom of God is as if a man should cast seed on the earth,

djk_text: Ne a de fi en a kondee. Neti ai siibi, dei ten a de fi en anga ain. Ma a sii goo sondee fu a man sabi fa a du goo.
eng_text: and should sleep and rise night and day, and the seed should spring up and grow, he doesn't know how.

djk_text: Ma, namo baka wan pisiten, ne den sii goo. Den booko ain kon a tapu doti, ne den goo, te puu boomiki meke nyanyan.
eng_text: For the earth bears fruit: first the blade, then the ear, then the full grain in the ear.

djk_text: Da, wanten wanten, di a sii meke nyanyan lepi, ne a goonman teke en babun nefi, ne a go koti den. Bika, a yuu fu koti den sii ya, be doo kaba.”
eng_text: But when the fruit is ripe, immediately he puts forth the sickle, because the harvest has come."

djk_text: Ne, Masaa Jesesi akisi den baka taki: “Sowtu ageisi toli mi sa teke soi u, fu u sa sabi fa a Nyun Tii fu Masaa Gadu de, moo?
eng_text: He said, "How will we liken the Kingdom of God? Or with what parable will we illustrate it?

djk_text: We, meke u taki: A de enke wan sii den e kai mosite. A sii ya na wan pikintoin sii.
eng_text: It's like a grain of mustard seed, which, when it is sown in the earth, though it is less than all the seeds that are on the earth,

djk_text: Ma, te den paandi en, te a goo, da ai bigi moo ala den taa sani di den paandi a ini a goon. Den ana fi en e bigi paati, te den foo e meke nesi e teke koo a den.”
eng_text: yet when it is sown, grows up, and becomes greater than all the herbs, and puts out great branches, so that the birds of the sky can lodge under its shadow."

djk_text: Da, te Masaa Jesesi be e gi den sama Gadu wowtu, da a be lobi teke den sowtu toli ya gi den sama. Da na a fasi ya, den be sa fusutan san a be wani leli den.
eng_text: With many such parables he spoke the word to them, as they were able to hear it.

djk_text: Da a á be e taki anga den sondee fu gi den, den sowtu toli ya. Ma, te en anga den bakaman fi en wawan be de, da a be e puu ala sani gi den fini fini.
eng_text: Without a parable he didn't speak to them; but privately to his own disciples he explained everything.

djk_text: Da, di sapaten doo, ne Masaa Jesesi taigi den bakaman fi en taki: “U kon meke u abaa go na abaase.”
eng_text: On that day, when evening had come, he said to them, "Let's go over to the other side."

djk_text: Ne den fika den somen sama wawan a baka, ne den go a boto anga Masaa Jesesi e go na abaase. Da, wantu taa boto be e koti abaa anga en tu.
eng_text: Leaving the multitude, they took him with them, even as he was, in the boat. Other small boats were also with him.

djk_text: Ma namo, wan gaan winta kisi den a pasi. Da a wataa be seke, meke gaan paana e wasi kon a ini a boto te. A boto fuu kwaa, pikinmoo den sungu.
eng_text: A big wind storm arose, and the waves beat into the boat, so much that the boat was already filled.

djk_text: Ma Masaa Jesesi be didon a bakase fu a boto, poti ede a wan kunsu e siibi. Ne den bakaman fi en weki en taki: “Mesiti! I á si taki, wi o dede kaba a soso, no? I ná abi toobi seefi taki, wi o dede, no?”
eng_text: He himself was in the stern, asleep on the cushion, and they woke him up, and told him, "Teacher, don't you care that we are dying?"

djk_text: Ne Masaa Jesesi opo, ne a kaasi a winta fu tan pii. Ne a taigi a ze taki: “Kaba! Tan pii!” Ne a winta tan pii. A ze seefi koo pii tu. A winta nái wai taanga moo, a ze nái seke moo.
eng_text: He awoke, and rebuked the wind, and said to the sea, "Peace! Be still!" The wind ceased, and there was a great calm.

djk_text: Ne Masaa Jesesi akisi den bakaman fi en taki: “Saide meke u feele so? U á poti fitoow a mi ete, no?”
eng_text: He said to them, "Why are you so afraid? How is it that you have no faith?"

djk_text: Ne den bakaman fu Masaa Jesesi feele, te den e akisi denseefi taki: “Sama na a sama ya seefi? A winta anga a ze seefi e teke en taki!”
eng_text: They were greatly afraid, and said to one another, "Who then is this, that even the wind and the sea obey him?"

djk_text: We, ne Masaa Jesesi anga den bakaman fi en go doo na abaase fu a ze fu Galileya. Ne den poti boto na a pisiwataa fu den Gelaseini sama.
eng_text: They came to the other side of the sea, into the country of the Gadarenes.

djk_text: Fa i si Masaa Jesesi komoto a soo, ne wan man lon kon ne en. Wan takuu jeje be de na a man ya tapu.
eng_text: When he had come out of the boat, immediately a man with an unclean spirit met him out of the tombs.

djk_text: Da na den siton geebi mindii a man ya be e tan. A be taanga te, ná wan sama be poi kisi en tei moo. Keti seefi á be poi keti en.
eng_text: He lived in the tombs. Nobody could bind him any more, not even with chains,

djk_text: Na onmen leisi den bui en ana anga en futu anga keti, ma a booko den keti enke lawlaw sani. Ná wan sama di be poi oli en.
eng_text: because he had been often bound with fetters and chains, and the chains had been torn apart by him, and the fetters broken in pieces. Nobody had the strength to tame him.

djk_text: Dei anga neti a man ya be de a ini a belipe anga den mongo mindii e waka e bali gaan balibali e naki enseefi koti anga siton.
eng_text: Always, night and day, in the tombs and in the mountains, he was crying out, and cutting himself with stones.

djk_text: Da, a man de, te a faawe si Masaa Jesesi, ne a go ne en. Ne a sutu kini a doti, a Masaa Jesesi fesi.
eng_text: When he saw Jesus from afar, he ran and bowed down to him,

djk_text: Ne a bali taki: “San mi anga yu abi nownow kaba, Jesesi, Pikin fu a moo Hei Gadu? Mi teke Gadu nen begi yu, ná sitaafu mi, baa!”
eng_text: and crying out with a loud voice, he said, "What have I to do with you, Jesus, you Son of the Most High God? I adjure you by God, don't torment me."

djk_text: Da, na fu di Masaa Jesesi be kaasi a takuu jeje, fu a gwe komoto na a man tapu wanten wanten, meke a be e bali so.
eng_text: For he said to him, "Come out of the man, you unclean spirit!"

djk_text: Ne Masaa Jesesi akisi en taki: “Fa den e kai yu nen?” Ne a takuu jeje piki taki: “Na mi den e kai Hipiman, bika u de ya anga tyaipi man.”
eng_text: He asked him, "What is your name?" He said to him, "My name is Legion, for we are many."

djk_text: Ne, den begi Masaa Jesesi taki: “Gaantangi, ná yaki u puu na a pisiwataa ya, baa!”
eng_text: He begged him much that he would not send them away out of the country.

djk_text: Da, somen somen agu be de a wan mongo koosube de, e suku sani fu nyan.
eng_text: Now on the mountainside there was a great herd of pigs feeding.

djk_text: Ne den takuu jeje begi Masaa Jesesi taki: “Te i puu wi na a sama ya, sende u go a ini den agu, baa!”
eng_text: All the demons begged him, saying, "Send us into the pigs, that we may enter into them."

djk_text: Ne Masaa Jesesi meke den go. Den takuu jeje komoto na man, ne den go a ini den agu. Ne wanten wanten, ne ala den tu dunsu agu lon saka a mongo hullu, te a ze dubuu. Ná wan di komoto moo. Ala fiya dede.
eng_text: At once Jesus gave them permission. The unclean spirits came out and entered into the pigs. The herd of about two thousand rushed down the steep bank into the sea, and they were drowned in the sea.

djk_text: Ne, den sama di be e luku den agu si san pasa, ne den lon gwe. Ne den paati a mofu na a hii kondee anga a pisiwataa de, fu san pasa. Da, na so den sama komoto kon luku san pasa.
eng_text: Those who fed them fled, and told it in the city and in the country. The people came to see what it was that had happened.

djk_text: Da, di den doo Masaa Jesesi, ne den si a man, di den tyaipi takuu jeje be de ne en tapu. A sidon de pii, wei koosi moi, de fi en anga en bunbun fusutan baka. Da, den sama feele fu san den si ya.
eng_text: They came to Jesus, and saw him who had been possessed by demons sitting, clothed, and in his right mind, even him who had the legion; and they were afraid.

djk_text: Den sama di be si, taigi sama san den si pasa anga a man, di den takuu jeje be de ne en tapu anga den agu.
eng_text: Those who saw it declared to them how it happened to him who was possessed by demons, and about the pigs.

djk_text: Ne, di den sama yee so, ne den bigin begi Masaa Jesesi gaantangi fu a komoto a den kondee de gwe.
eng_text: They began to beg him to depart from their region.

djk_text: Ne, fa i si Masaa Jesesi go a boto baka, ne a man, di den takuu jeje be de ne en tapu begi en taki: “Meke mi go anga yu, baa?”
eng_text: As he was entering into the boat, he who had been possessed by demons begged him that he might be with him.

djk_text: Ma, Masaa Jesesi á gi pasi fu dati. Pe fu dati, ne a taigi a man taki: “Nono! Go a osu a den sama fi yu, da taigi den san Masaa du gi yu, anga fa a be abi tyali ati fi yu.”
eng_text: He didn't allow him, but said to him, "Go to your house, to your friends, and tell them what great things the Lord has done for you, and how he had mercy on you."

djk_text: Ne a man go. Ne ai paati a mofu fu san di Masaa Jesesi du gi en na a hii pisi kondee di den e kai Dekapolisi . Da ala sama be e foondoo fu a sani ya.
eng_text: He went his way, and began to proclaim in Decapolis how Jesus had done great things for him, and everyone marveled.

djk_text: Ne Masaa Jesesi abaa a ze fu Galileya baka go na abaase. Da somen sama kon ne en a wataa mofu te a ipi.
eng_text: When Jesus had crossed back over in the boat to the other side, a great multitude was gathered to him; and he was by the sea.

djk_text: Wan man den e kai Yailesi seefi kon a Masaa Jesesi tu. Di a si Masaa Jesesi, ne, wanten a sutu kini a doti ne en fesi. Yailesi na be wan fu den edeman fu Dyu keliki.
eng_text: Behold, one of the rulers of the synagogue, Jairus by name, came; and seeing him, he fell at his feet,

djk_text: Ne a begi Masaa Jesesi taki: “Masaa Jesesi! Wan pikin umanpikin fu mi e dede, baa. Gaantangi, kon poti yu ana ne en tapu, gi mi baa, fu a kon bun baka, da a o libi!”
eng_text: and begged him much, saying, "My little daughter is at the point of death. Please come and lay your hands on her, that she may be made healthy, and live."

djk_text: Ne Masaa Jesesi e go anga en. Da, somen sama be e kon a Masaa Jesesi baka. Den be e toto fu ala se e kon ne en.
eng_text: He went with him, and a great multitude followed him, and they pressed upon him on all sides.

djk_text: Ma, wan uman be de a ini den somen sama de di be abi wan lasi buulu siki. Twalufu yali kaba, di a be kisi en, sondee fu koti.
eng_text: A certain woman, who had an issue of blood for twelve years,

djk_text: Anga ala fa a uman ya, be pai anga ala a moni di a be abi fu suku yeepi a somen somen dataa, toku a á be poi fende yeepi. Pe fu dati, ne na moo a siki be e moo ogii.
eng_text: and had suffered many things by many physicians, and had spent all that she had, and was no better, but rather grew worse,

djk_text: Ma fanafu di a uman ya yee den sani di Masaa Jesesi e du, ne a waka ne en baka a ini den somen sama, ne a oli en koosi.
eng_text: having heard the things concerning Jesus, came up behind him in the crowd, and touched his clothes.

djk_text: Bika a be e taki a ini enseefi taki: “Efu mi sa lobi ana ne en koosi namo, mi sa kon bun.”
eng_text: For she said, "If I just touch his clothes, I will be made well."

djk_text: Ne wanten, a buulu koti. Ne a fii a ini en sikin taki, a kon bun fu den pina fu ala den yali.
eng_text: Immediately the flow of her blood was dried up, and she felt in her body that she was healed of her affliction.

djk_text: Ne a seefi yuu de, ne Masaa Jesesi fii kaakiti e komoto ne en sikin go deesi wan sama. Ne a daai a ini den somen sama, ne a akisi taki: “Sama meli mi koosi?”
eng_text: Immediately Jesus, perceiving in himself that the power had gone out from him, turned around in the crowd, and asked, "Who touched my clothes?"

djk_text: Ne, den bakaman fi en taigi en taki: “Masaa Jesesi, fa i sa akisi sama meli yu? Luku onmen sama e toto yu fu ala se ya.”
eng_text: His disciples said to him, "You see the multitude pressing against you, and you say, 'Who touched me?'"

djk_text: Ma, ai daai e luku fu si a sama di meli en.
eng_text: He looked around to see her who had done this thing.

djk_text: Ne a uman kon a fesi anga ala feele anga dansi sikin. Bika a sabi san pasa anga en seefi. Ne a saka kini a Masaa Jesesi fesi, ne a taigi en pilisisi ala san pasa anga en, di a oli en.
eng_text: But the woman, fearing and trembling, knowing what had been done to her, came and fell down before him, and told him all the truth.

djk_text: Ne, Masaa Jesesi taigi en taki: “Uman! A biibi fi yu yeepi yu fi i kon bun baka. Go baka a osu anga koo ati! A gaan pina siki wai pasa gwe.”
eng_text: He said to her, "Daughter, your faith has made you well. Go in peace, and be cured of your disease."

djk_text: Da, a ten di Masaa Jesesi e taki anga a uman ya ete, ne wantu sama komoto a Yailesi osu tyai mofu kon. Den taigi Yailesi taki: “A pikin umanpikin fi yu dede. A á de fi i muliki a mesiti fu a go anda moo.”
eng_text: While he was still speaking, people came from the synagogue ruler's house saying, "Your daughter is dead. Why bother the Teacher any more?"

djk_text: Ma, Masaa Jesesi yee, di den gi Yailesi a bosikopu. Ne a taigi Yailesi taki: “Ná feele! Ma biibi namo.”
eng_text: But Jesus, when he heard the message spoken, immediately said to the ruler of the synagogue, "Don't be afraid, only believe."

djk_text: Ma, boiti Peitilisi anga Jakowbesi anga Johanisi, da Masaa Jesesi á meke ná wan sama go anga en moo a Yailesi osu.
eng_text: He allowed no one to follow him, except Peter, James, and John the brother of James.

djk_text: Da, di den doo Yailesi osu, ne Masaa Jesesi si soso kee anga balibali de. Sama e kee e bali, te ná sipowtu.
eng_text: He came to the synagogue ruler's house, and he saw an uproar, weeping, and great wailing.

djk_text: Ne, di Masaa Jesesi go a ini a osu, ne a akisi den taki: “Saide meke u e kee e bali so du? A pikin á dede! Na siibi namo ai siibi!”
eng_text: When he had entered in, he said to them, "Why do you make an uproar and weep? The child is not dead, but is asleep."

djk_text: Ne, den sama kii en anga lafu. Ma, Masaa Jesesi poti ala den fiya a doo. Ne, a teke a dda anga a mma fu a pikin anga den dii bakaman fi en, ne den go a pe a pikin de.
eng_text: They ridiculed him. But he, having put them all out, took the father of the child, her mother, and those who were with him, and went in where the child was lying.

djk_text: Ne Masaa Jesesi oli a pikin ana, ne a taigi en taki: “
eng_text: Taking the child by the hand, he said to her, "Talitha cumi!" which means, being interpreted, "Girl, I tell you, get up!"

djk_text: Ne wanten wanten, ne a pikin umanpikin opo, ne a bigin e waka e lontu a ini a osu. Da a pikin abi twalufu yali kaba. Da a sani, di pasa ya bigi gi den sama, te ná sipowtu.
eng_text: Immediately the girl rose up and walked, for she was twelve years old. They were amazed with great amazement.

djk_text: Ne, Masaa Jesesi bali den taanga taanga fu den á meke ná wan sama sabi san pasa de. Soseefi tu a taigi den fu den gi a pikin sani fu nyan.
eng_text: He strictly ordered them that no one should know this, and commanded that something should be given to her to eat.

djk_text: Masaa Jesesi komoto de, ne a go ne en eigi kondee. Da den bakaman fi en go anga en tu.
eng_text: He went out from there. He came into his own country, and his disciples followed him.

djk_text: Ne, di a kina dei fu den Dyu doo, ne a bigin fu leli sama Masaa Gadu wowtu a ini a Dyu keliki. Somen sama, di yee en, foondoo, te den e akisi taki: “Pe a man ya komoto, a anga den sani di ai leli de? Pe a fende a koni de? Sama gi en a kaakiti fu ai du den gaan foondoo wooko di wi yee ai du?
eng_text: When the Sabbath had come, he began to teach in the synagogue, and many hearing him were astonished, saying, "Where did this man get these things?" and, "What is the wisdom that is given to this man, that such mighty works come about by his hands?

djk_text: A ná a tembeeman de ya, no? A ná a pikin fu Maliya, no? U sabi den baala fi en bunbun, Jakowbesi, Jowsef, Judasi anga Simon. A ná wi anga den sisa fi en e tan a Nasaleti ya, no?” Da na so den teke en fu ogii. Den ná abi bisi anga en.
eng_text: Isn't this the carpenter, the son of Mary, and brother of James, Joses, Judah, and Simon? Aren't his sisters here with us?" They were offended at him.

djk_text: Ma Masaa Jesesi piki den taki: “Ala sama fu goontapu e lesipeki wan apaiti takiman fu Masaa Gadu, ma den sama fi en eigi kondee seefi, en eigi famii anga den sama fi en eigi osu ini, nái lesipeki en.”
eng_text: Jesus said to them, "A prophet is not without honor, except in his own country, and among his own relatives, and in his own house."

djk_text: A á be poi du ná wan foondoo sani de, boiti taki a poti ana a wantu sikiman tapu deesi den.
eng_text: He could do no mighty work there, except that he laid his hands on a few sick people, and healed them.

djk_text: Da, a be foondoo Masaa Jesesi, fu di den sama fi en eigi kondee á be wani poti biibi ne en. Ne a komoto de go a wantu taa kondee na a seefi pisiwataa de, go e leli sama Masaa Gadu wowtu.
eng_text: He marveled because of their unbelief. He went around the villages teaching.

djk_text: Ne wan dei, ne a kai den twalufu apaiti bosikopuman fi en kon, ne a sende den, tu tu man, fu den go a den kondee kondee go paati Masaa Gadu wowtu. Ne a taigi den taki: “U go! Mi gi u taanga fu u puu takuu jeje a sama tapu.
eng_text: He called to himself the twelve, and began to send them out two by two; and he gave them authority over the unclean spirits.

djk_text: Ma, te u e go, u á mu tyai ná wan enkii taa sani moo enke wan waka tiki namo a u ana. U á mu tyai beele. U á lai tasi tyai.
eng_text: He commanded them that they should take nothing for their journey, except a staff only: no bread, no wallet, no money in their purse,

djk_text: U á mu tyai taa susu anga koosi. Den di u wei de sai kaba.”
eng_text: but to wear sandals, and not put on two tunics.

djk_text: Ne Masaa Jesesi taigi den taki: “Di u o go, te u go a wan osu, da u mu tan de, te enke u kaba fu gwe baka.
eng_text: He said to them, "Wherever you enter into a house, stay there until you depart from there.

djk_text: Da, te u doo wan peesi pe sama á wani teke u a den osu efu aliki a bosikopu di u e tyai. Da u mu gwe. Ma fosi u gwe, da u mu naki u futu puu a santi meke den sabi taki den be fende a okasi fu aliki a Bun Nyunsu fu mi. Da a fika gi den.”
eng_text: Whoever will not receive you nor hear you, as you depart from there, shake off the dust that is under your feet for a testimony against them. Assuredly, I tell you, it will be more tolerable for Sodom and Gomorrah in the day of judgment than for that city!"

djk_text: Da, na so den bakaman fu Masaa Jesesi gwe. Ne den go a den kondee kondee go e bali den sama taki, meke den daai libi.
eng_text: They went out and preached that people should repent.

djk_text: Da, den yaki somen takuu jeje puu a sama tapu. Soseefi den lobi oli a somen sikisama sikin deesi den kon bun baka.
eng_text: They cast out many demons, and anointed many with oil who were sick, and healed them.

djk_text: Da Kownu Helowdesi seefi yee fu den sani di Masaa Jesesi e du. Bika Masaa Jesesi nen be bali na ala peesi. Son sama taki: “Johanisi a Dopuman weki komoto a dede kon a libi baka. A dati meke a abi a kaakiti fu du den gaan foondoo foondoo sani ya.”
eng_text: King Herod heard this, for his name had become known, and he said, "John the Baptizer has risen from the dead, and therefore these powers are at work in him."

djk_text: Taawan taki: “Na Eliya! Ne en de ya.” Taawan taki: “Na wan apaiti takiman fu Masaa Gadu, enke wan fu den fositen apaiti takiman.”
eng_text: But others said, "He is Elijah." Others said, "He is a prophet, or like one of the prophets."

djk_text: Ma, di Kownu Helowdesi seefi yee a sani ya, ne a taki: “Na Johanisi di mi be meke den kii, ne weki komoto a dede tuu.”
eng_text: But Herod, when he heard this, said, "This is John, whom I beheaded. He has risen from the dead."

djk_text: Bika, Kownu Helowdesi be meke den kisi Johanisi tei poti a dunguu osu. Da, na fu Helowdiya ede meke a du dati. Bika a be libi anga Helowdiya. Helowdiya na be a uman fu Filipi, a baala fu Helowdesi.
eng_text: For Herod himself had sent out and arrested John, and bound him in prison for the sake of Herodias, his brother Philip's wife, for he had married her.

djk_text: Da Johanisi be e bali Helowdesi taki, a á bun fu a teke a uman fi en baala libi.
eng_text: For John said to Herod, "It is not lawful for you to have your brother's wife."

djk_text: Da, di Helowdiya yee taki na so Johanisi bali Kownu Helowdesi, ne wan takuu atiboon teke en. A be wani kii Johanisi wanten wanten. Ma den á gi en pasi fu du dati,
eng_text: Herodias set herself against him, and desired to kill him, but she couldn't,

djk_text: bika Kownu Helowdesi be sabi taki Johanisi na be wan sama, di e libi letiopu fasi gi Masaa Gadu. Da a be e feele en. A dati meke a teke Johanisi poti a wan peesi pe sama á be sa fende en kii. Te a be e taki anga Johanisi, en konsensi be e fonmi en, ma toku, a be lobi aliki Johanisi.
eng_text: for Herod feared John, knowing that he was a righteous and holy man, and kept him safe. When he heard him, he did many things, and he heard him gladly.

djk_text: Na so den de, te wan dei, ne Helowdiya fende pasi fu kii Johanisi. Bika wan dei, Helowdesi oli wan gaan fuuyali piisii fi en a ini en paleisi. Da a be kai ala den sama di e wooko ne en ondoo, den edeman fu suudati den hei hei man fu Galileya.
eng_text: Then a convenient day came, that Herod on his birthday made a supper for his nobles, the high officers, and the chief men of Galilee.

djk_text: Ma namo, di den de na fesa, te wan pisi, ne a pikin umanpikin fu Helowdiya kon a pe Helowdesi anga ala den taa sama sidon. Ne a dansi de walla. Da fa a dansi so, a switi gi Kownu Helowdesi anga den taa man te, ná sipowtu. Ne Kownu Helowdesi taigi a pikin taki: “Mama! Akisi mi san i wani! Mi sa gi yu en.”
eng_text: When the daughter of Herodias herself came in and danced, she pleased Herod and those sitting with him. The king said to the young lady, "Ask me whatever you want, and I will give it to you."

djk_text: Ne Helowdesi taigi en go doo taki: “Mi e sweli taki, ibii sani di i akisi mi, mi o gi yu en. Efu na afu fu a kondee di mi e tii enke kownu ya seefi i wani, mi o gi yu en.”
eng_text: He swore to her, "Whatever you shall ask of me, I will give you, up to half of my kingdom."

djk_text: Ne a pikin umanpikin go a doose ne en mma. Ne a akisi en taki: “Mi mma, san mi mu akisi en?” Ne Helowdiya taigi en taki: “Piki Kownu taki i wani a ede fu Johanisi a Dopuman.”
eng_text: She went out, and said to her mother, "What shall I ask?" She said, "The head of John the Baptizer."

djk_text: Di en mma taigi en so, ne wanten wanten a lon go baka a Kownu Helowdesi baka. Ne a taigi en taki: “Mi wani i gi mi a ede fu Johanisi a Dopuman nownow de a ini wan gaan teepala.”
eng_text: She came in immediately with haste to the king, and asked, "I want you to give me right now the head of John the Baptizer on a platter."

djk_text: Da, di kownu yee so, ne gaan tyali kisi. Ma na fu a sweli, di a be meke a den bigiman de fesi gi a pikin umanpikin kaba, meke a á be poi puu a mofu de moo.
eng_text: The king was exceedingly sorry, but for the sake of his oaths, and of his dinner guests, he didn't wish to refuse her.

djk_text: Ne wanten, ne a sende wan fu den man suudati go koti a ede fu Johanisi tyai kon. Ne a man go, ne a doo Johanisi ede felen a ini a sitaafu osu.
eng_text: Immediately the king sent out a soldier of his guard, and commanded to bring John's head, and he went and beheaded him in the prison,

djk_text: Ne a tyai en kon a ini wan teepala. Ne a gi a pikin umanpikin. Ne a pikin umanpikin teke, ne a gi en mma.
eng_text: and brought his head on a platter, and gave it to the young lady; and the young lady gave it to her mother.

djk_text: Da, di den bakaman fu Johanisi yee taki den kii Johanisi, ne den go teke a dede sikin fu Johanisi go beli.
eng_text: When his disciples heard this, they came and took up his corpse, and laid it in a tomb.

djk_text: Da den twalufu apaiti bosikopuman fu Masaa Jesesi di a be sende gwe a den peesi peesi daai kon baka. Da den bigin fu taigi Masaa Jesesi ala san den du anga san den be leli den sama fu den peesi peesi pe a be sende den go.
eng_text: The apostles gathered themselves together to Jesus, and they told him all things, whatever they had done, and whatever they had taught.

djk_text: Ne Masaa Jesesi taigi den taki: “U kon meke u go a wan koo peesi pe sama á de go boo u sikin afu.” Bika somen sama be komoto a den kondee kondee e kon ne en namo e kon e suku yeepi, te den á be abi ten fu nyan wan bun fasi seefi. A dati meke a be wani go anga den bakaman fi en wawan a wan peesi. Ne den go a boto, ne den puu gwe.
eng_text: He said to them, "You come apart into a deserted place, and rest awhile." For there were many coming and going, and they had no leisure so much as to eat.

djk_text: Da somen sama si di den e puu gwe, ne den sabi kaba taki na sowan peesi sowan peesi den e go. Ne den lon a soo anga futu, fu te na a peesi pe Masaa Jesesi anga den bakaman fi en e go.
eng_text: They saw them going, and many recognized him and ran there on foot from all the cities. They arrived before them and came together to him.

djk_text: Da den sama doo fika Masaa Jesesi anga den bakaman fi en seefi. Da di den koosube di Masaa Jesesi luku, ne a si wataa mofu baaka pii anga libisama. Da tyali fu den sama kisi Masaa Jesesi. Bika den sama be gei sikapu di ná abi tiiman. A dati meke a leli den sani fu Masaa Gadu.
eng_text: Jesus came out, saw a great multitude, and he had compassion on them, because they were like sheep without a shepherd, and he began to teach them many things.

djk_text: Da di bakadina fosi neti kai, ne den bakaman fi en taigi en taki: “We, Masaa Jesesi ai lati namo.
eng_text: When it was late in the day, his disciples came to him, and said, "This place is deserted, and it is late in the day.

djk_text: Da sende den sama gwe. Da den sa bai sani fu nyan a den pikin pikin kondee. Bika ná wan sama e tan ya, da sani á de ya fu bai tu.”
eng_text: Send them away, that they may go into the surrounding country and villages, and buy themselves bread, for they have nothing to eat."

djk_text: Ma Masaa Jesesi piki den taki: “Nono! U gi den nyanyan meke den nyan.” Ne den bakaman fi en akisi en taki: “We, u ná abi beele fu gi den somen sama ya. I wani meke u go bai beele gi den? A o dii fu u mu bai nyanyan gi ala den somen sama ya.”
eng_text: But he answered them, "You give them something to eat." They asked him, "Shall we go and buy two hundred denarii worth of bread, and give them something to eat?"

djk_text: Ne Masaa Jesesi akisi den taki: “Onmen beele u abi de?” Ne den luku, ne den taki: “U abi feifi beele anga tu fisi ya.”
eng_text: He said to them, "How many loaves do you have? Go see." When they knew, they said, "Five, and two fish."

djk_text: Ne Masaa Jesesi taigi den sama taki meke den saka sidon a kulu ini a gaasi.
eng_text: He commanded them that everyone should sit down in groups on the green grass.

djk_text: Fa i si Masaa Jesesi kaba taigi den so, ne den sidon a ini kulu fu wan ondoo anga kulu fu feifitenti sama.
eng_text: They sat down in ranks, by hundreds and by fifties.

djk_text: Ne a teke den feifi beele anga den tu fisi. Ne a luku tapu a Masaa Gadu, ne a gi Masaa Gadu daa moi te a kaba. Ne a booko den beele pisipisi anga tu fisi. Ne a gi den bakaman fi en, fu den go paati. Da soseefi a meke den paati den fisi tu.
eng_text: He took the five loaves and the two fish, and looking up to heaven, he blessed and broke the loaves, and he gave to his disciples to set before them, and he divided the two fish among them all.

djk_text: Ne ala sama nyan te den bee fuu.
eng_text: They all ate, and were filled.

djk_text: Da di den bakaman fu Masaa Jesesi piki san di den nyan fika, ne a fuu twalufu bakisi.
eng_text: They took up twelve baskets full of broken pieces and also of the fish.

djk_text: Da fu den manengee wawan di be nyan, da a moo enke feifi dunsu.
eng_text: Those who ate the loaves were five thousand men.

djk_text: Ne wanten bakadati, ne Masaa Jesesi taigi den bakaman fi en, fu go a boto koti abaa go na abaase a Betisaida. Ma en o fika de, fu sende den sama gwe a den osu.
eng_text: Immediately he made his disciples get into the boat, and to go ahead to the other side, to Bethsaida, while he himself sent the multitude away.

djk_text: Ne di a sende ala den sama gwe kaba, ne a subi go a wan mongo tapu, go e begi.
eng_text: After he had taken leave of them, he went up the mountain to pray.

djk_text: A yuu ten de, da peesi be kon e dunguu kaba. Ma, den bakaman fi en be de, te a mindii wataa kaba anga a boto. Ne en wawan be de a soo ete.
eng_text: When evening had come, the boat was in the midst of the sea, and he was alone on the land.

djk_text: Ne di a begi te wan pisi, di a daai luku, ne a si taki den de a mindii fu a ze ete e feti anga a boto. Den e puu ma den nái go a fesi. Wan gaan winta e wai na a ze, meke den á poi go a fesi. Namo di musude, ne Masaa Jesesi waka na a wataa tapu tyaa tyaa go miti den. Da a waka enke a be wani pasa den.
eng_text: Seeing them distressed in rowing, for the wind was contrary to them, about the fourth watch of the night he came to them, walking on the sea, and he would have passed by them,

djk_text: Da di den si a sama e waka na a ze tapu anga futu e kon, ne den feele te den bigin bali. Den be denki taki na wan yooka e kon a den. Ne Masaa Jesesi bali gi den taki: “U á feele! U oli useefi. Na mi de ya!”
eng_text: but they, when they saw him walking on the sea, supposed that it was a ghost, and cried out;

djk_text: Ne a subi go a ini a boto a den. Da di a subi go a ini a boto, ne a winta saka wanten wanten. Den foondoo te, den fika opo opo mofu.
eng_text: He got into the boat with them; and the wind ceased, and they were very amazed among themselves, and marveled;

djk_text: Da anga ala fa den be si Masaa Jesesi be paati feifi beele anga tu fisi gi onmen dunsu sama, toku den á be wani fusutan ete sama Masaa Jesesi be de.
eng_text: for they hadn't understood about the loaves, but their hearts were hardened.

djk_text: Ne den poti boto a Genesaleti, ne den go a soo.
eng_text: When they had crossed over, they came to land at Gennesaret, and moored to the shore.

djk_text: Da fa i si den poti futu a soo, ne den sama di be de a lampe sabi kaba taki a man ya, na Masaa Jesesi, di e deesi ala sowtu siki.
eng_text: When they had come out of the boat, immediately the people recognized him,

djk_text: Ne den lon lontu kondee paati a mofu te a doo. Ne den sama tyai ala den sikiman kon a Masaa Jesesi.
eng_text: and ran around that whole region, and began to bring those who were sick, on their mats, to where they heard he was.

djk_text: Da ibiiwan peesi pe Masaa Jesesi be go, efu na pikin kondee efu wan foto efu na pikin kampu seefi, da den sama be e tyai siki sama kon poti a ganda a pe a be o waka pasa. Da den e begi en taki: “Gaantangi, meke den sama oli i koosi mofu, baa! Da den sa kon bun baka.” Namo, da ala siki sama di be oli kon bun kelle.
eng_text: Wherever he entered, into villages, or into cities, or into the country, they laid the sick in the marketplaces, and begged him that they might touch just the fringe of his garment; and as many as touched him were made well.

djk_text: Da wan dei, ne den Faliseiman anga wantu leliman fu Dyuweiti komoto a Jelusalem Foto kon a Masaa Jesesi.
eng_text: Then the Pharisees, and some of the scribes gathered together to him, having come from Jerusalem.

djk_text: Te wan pisi, ne den si taki, te son fu den bakaman fu Masaa Jesesi e nyan, da den nái wasi ana na a fasi fa den Dyu gwenti fu wasi ana na a apaiti fasi fosi den go nyan.
eng_text: Now when they saw some of his disciples eating bread with defiled, that is, unwashed, hands, they found fault.

djk_text: Den Faliseiman anga ala den taa Dyusama á be e nyan fosi den wasi den ana a wan apaiti fasi enke fa den gaansama fu den leli den taki,
eng_text: (For the Pharisees, and all the Jews, don't eat unless they wash their hands and forearms, holding to the tradition of the elders.

djk_text: te den komoto a wowoyo kon, den á mu nyan fosi den wasi a wan apaiti fasi. Da den be e oli somen fu den weiti ete, di den avo gaansama fika gi den. Den be mu wasi den tyobo sani a wan apaiti fasi tu. Den sani enke den kan fu diingi wataa, den patu, beenki fu nyan.
eng_text: They don't eat when they come from the marketplace, unless they bathe themselves, and there are many other things, which they have received to hold to: washings of cups, pitchers, bronze vessels, and couches.)

djk_text: Ne den Faliseiman anga den leliman fu Dyuweiti akisi Masaa Jesesi taki: “Saide meke den bakaman fi yu nái oli den weiti di den gaansama poti gi wi. Bika den e nyan sondee fu wasi den ana na a apaiti fasi.”
eng_text: The Pharisees and the scribes asked him, "Why don't your disciples walk according to the tradition of the elders, but eat their bread with unwashed hands?"

djk_text: Ne Masaa Jesesi taigi den taki: “U bidiigiman u! Jesaja, a apaiti takiman fu Masaa Gadu, be abi leti di a be sikiifi fu u a Gadu Buku taki: ‘Den sama ya e lesipeki mi e gi mi gaandi anga den buba mofu, ma a nái doo den ati. Den pakisei de faawe fu mi.
eng_text: He answered them, "Well did Isaiah prophesy of you hypocrites, as it is written, 'This people honors me with their lips, but their heart is far from me.

djk_text: Fa den e bali e hei mi anga den buba mofu de, ná tuu. Bika ná den weiti fu mi den e leli sama. Ma na weiti di libisama seefi meke den e leli sama.’
eng_text: But in vain do they worship me, teaching as doctrines the commandments of men.'

djk_text: U poti den weiti fu Masaa Gadu a wanse, da u e teke den weiti di libisama meke fu gaan sani fu wooko.”
eng_text: For you set aside the commandment of God, and hold tightly to the tradition of men--the washing of pitchers and cups, and you do many other such things.

djk_text: Ne Masaa Jesesi taigi den go doo taki: “U ná abi toobi fu poti den weiti fu Masaa Gadu a wanse, soso fu u oli den haw gwenti fu u.
eng_text: He said to them, "Full well do you reject the commandment of God, that you may keep your tradition.

djk_text: Mi o taigi u san a avo gaansama fu u di den be e kai Mosesi be sikiifi a Gadu Buku. A be sikiifi taki: ‘U mu lesipeki u dda anga u mma. Da iniiwan sama di kosi en mma efu en dda mu dede.’
eng_text: For Moses said, 'Honor your father and your mother;' and, 'He who speaks evil of father or mother, let him be put to death.'

djk_text: Ma u daai a weiti fu Masaa Gadu ya poti taki: ‘I ná abi fu yeepi i mma anga i dda, fu gi den sani moo, efi i taigi den taki, san i be o gi den, i paamisi fu gi Masaa Gadu dati enke paiman.’
eng_text: But you say, 'If a man tells his father or his mother, "Whatever profit you might have received from me is Corban , that is to say, given to God";'

djk_text: Da efu wan sama taki so, da u nái gi en pasi fu yeepi en mma anga en dda a sani moo. Da san u du ya e soi taki u ná abi fu abi toobi anga Masaa Gadu wowtu moo. U wani meke den sama oli den weiti di den avo gaansama fu u fika gi u. Da a fasi fu libi ya e meke u poli a weiti fu Masaa Gadu. Da somen taa sani de tu di u e du na a seefi fasi.”
eng_text: then you no longer allow him to do anything for his father or his mother,

djk_text: Ne Masaa Jesesi kai ala den sama kon, ne a taigi den taki: “U aliki mi bun! San mi o taigi u ya, na wan sani di u musu fu sabi.
eng_text: He called all the multitude to himself, and said to them, "Hear me, all of you, and understand.

djk_text: Wan sama nái tyobo a Masaa Gadu fesi fu san di ai nyan go a ini en bee. Ma na den sani di ai taki komoto a ini en mofu ini kon a doo, na den e meke a tyobo a Gadu fesi.
eng_text: There is nothing from outside of the man, that going into him can defile him; but the things which proceed out of the man are those that defile the man.

djk_text: Meke sama di abi yesi fu yee, yee san mi taki ya!”
eng_text: If anyone has ears to hear, let him hear!"

djk_text: Da di Masaa Jesesi taigi den so kaba, ne a fika den, ne a go a ini wan osu. Ne den bakaman fi en akisi en taki: “San wani taki a toli di i gi den sama de?”
eng_text: When he had entered into a house away from the multitude, his disciples asked him about the parable.

djk_text: Ne Masaa Jesesi piki den taki: “Na so useefi don fu fusutan sani enke den taa sama de?
eng_text: He said to them, "Are you thus without understanding also? Don't you perceive that whatever goes into the man from outside can't defile him,

djk_text: We, a nyanyan di yu e nyan, nái go a yu ati, ma ai go a ini yu bee. Da te a yuu doo, da ai komoto baka.” Da anga disi Masaa Jesesi be wani taigi den taki, den á mu oli kina moo, ma den sa nyan ala san di de fu nyan sondee konsensi fonfon.
eng_text: because it doesn't go into his heart, but into his stomach, then into the latrine, thus purifying all foods ?"

djk_text: Ne a taki go doo taki: “Na den sani di e komoto a u ati e meke u kon tyobo a Masaa Gadu fesi.
eng_text: He said, "That which proceeds out of the man, that defiles the man.

djk_text: Den sani enke motyo libi, fufuu anga kii sama, go a taa man ofu taa uman.
eng_text: For from within, out of the hearts of men, proceed evil thoughts, adulteries, sexual sins, murders, thefts,

djk_text: Den sani enke giili ati anga takuu fasi, koli sama, fanya libi, dyalusu, saanti sama, bigi fasi anga lawlaw denki.
eng_text: covetings, wickedness, deceit, lustful desires, an evil eye, blasphemy, pride, and foolishness.

djk_text: Na den sani ya de a ini wan sama ati. Da te den e komoto a doo, da den e meke a sama tyobo a Masaa Gadu fesi.”
eng_text: All these evil things come from within, and defile the man."

djk_text: Da di Masaa Jesesi taigi den so, ne a komoto de, ne a go a Tilosi. Da di a doo Tilosi, ne a go a ini wan osu. A á be wani meke sama sabi taki a be de ape. Ma Masaa Jesesi á poi de a wan peesi, da a tan kibii.
eng_text: From there he arose, and went away into the borders of Tyre and Sidon. He entered into a house, and didn't want anyone to know it, but he couldn't escape notice.

djk_text: Bika a á be de ape langa seefi fosi wan uman kon ne en. Da a uman ya be abi wan pikin umanpikin di be abi wan sani ne en tapu. Da fa i si a uman ya doo Masaa Jesesi, ne a sutu kini a doti
eng_text: For a woman, whose little daughter had an unclean spirit, having heard of him, came and fell down at his feet.

djk_text: e begi en fu a puu a takuu jeje na a pikin fi en tapu. A uman ya na be wan Giiki sama di be meke na a kondee di den e kai Silofenisi.
eng_text: Now the woman was a Greek, a Syrophoenician by race. She begged him that he would cast the demon out of her daughter.

djk_text: Ma Masaa Jesesi piki en anga wan ageisi toli taki: “A á bun fu teke a nyanyan fu den pikin towe gi pikin dagu. Meke den pikin fosi nyan.”
eng_text: But Jesus said to her, "Let the children be filled first, for it is not appropriate to take the children's bread and throw it to the dogs."

djk_text: Ne a uman piki Masaa Jesesi taki: “Masaa san i taki na tuu. Ma den pikin dagu e nyan den sakasaka di den pikin e nyan towe a doti.”
eng_text: But she answered him, "Yes, Lord. Yet even the dogs under the table eat the children's crumbs."

djk_text: Ne Masaa Jesesi piki a uman taki: “A bun! Fu di i piki sowan fasi, meke i fende yeepi. Go a osu baka! A pikin umanpikin fi yu kon bun. A takuu jeje komoto ne en tapu.” Na so a uman daai go a osu.
eng_text: He said to her, "For this saying, go your way. The demon has gone out of your daughter."

djk_text: Di a doo osu, ne a si a pikin fi en didon a kama tapu pii. A takuu jeje gwe komoto ne en tapu gwe. A kon bun kelle.
eng_text: She went away to her house, and found the child having been laid on the bed, with the demon gone out.

djk_text: Namo Masaa Jesesi komoto a Tilosi waka go a Sidon. Ne a waka go na a pisi di den e kai Dekapolisi na abaase fu a ze fu Galileya.
eng_text: Again he departed from the borders of Tyre and Sidon, and came to the sea of Galilee, through the midst of the region of Decapolis.

djk_text: Ne di a doo de, ne den tyai wan man kon ne en. A man ya be dofu. Ma soseefi, a di na sani, ne a be e taki. Ne den sama begi Masaa Jesesi fu a poti ana na a man ya tapu meke a kon bun.
eng_text: They brought to him one who was deaf and had an impediment in his speech. They begged him to lay his hand on him.

djk_text: Ne Masaa Jesesi tyai a man ya puu a ini den somen sama go a wanse. Ne a toosi en finga go a ini a man yesi. Ne a puu en ana baka, ne a towe wataa mofu ne en ana, ne a nama ana na a man tongo.
eng_text: He took him aside from the multitude, privately, and put his fingers into his ears, and he spat, and touched his tongue.

djk_text: Ne Masaa Jesesi luku tapu, ne a ali wan dipi boo. Ne a taki: “
eng_text: Looking up to heaven, he sighed, and said to him, "Ephphatha!" that is, "Be opened!"

djk_text: Ne wanten wanten so a man yesi opo woo, ne ai yee sani bun. Da soseefi en tongo losi te ai taki wala wala enke fa wan libisama meke fu taki.
eng_text: Immediately his ears were opened, and the impediment of his tongue was released, and he spoke clearly.

djk_text: Ne Masaa Jesesi bali den sama taki: “U á mu taigi sama taki na mi deesi a man ya, u yee!” Ma anga ala fa a bali den de, toku den e taigi sama taki: “Na Masaa Jesesi deesi a man! Na Masaa Jesesi deesi!”
eng_text: He commanded them that they should tell no one, but the more he commanded them, so much the more widely they proclaimed it.

djk_text: Den á be poi tan pii fu san den si Masaa Jesesi du. A be foondoo den. Den e bali taki: “Ala den sani fiya di Masaa Jesesi e du ai du bun. Ai opo dofuman yesi. Ai losi babaw tongo fu den taki tu.”
eng_text: They were astonished beyond measure, saying, "He has done all things well. He makes even the deaf hear, and the mute speak!"

djk_text: Da somen sama be kon aliki Masaa Jesesi. Den ná abi sani fu nyan. Ne Masaa Jesesi kai den bakaman fi en, ne a taigi den taki:
eng_text: In those days, when there was a very great multitude, and they had nothing to eat, Jesus called his disciples to himself, and said to them,

djk_text: “Tyali fu den sama e kisi mi. Den de ya dii dei anga mi kaba. Da den ná abi ná wan sani fu nyan.
eng_text:
I have compassion on the multitude, because they have stayed with me now three days, and have nothing to eat.
1347	Efu mi sende den go a osu so, den sa faaw a pasi fu a angii. Somen fu den e tan faawe.”	1347	If I send them away fasting to their home, they will faint on the way, for some of them have come a long way.

djk_text: Ne den bakaman fi en akisi en taki: “Pe u o fende nyanyan a ini a sabana ya, pe ná wan sama e tan, fu gi ala den somen sama ya?”
eng_text: His disciples answered him, "From where could one satisfy these people with bread here in a deserted place?"

djk_text: Ne Masaa Jesesi akisi den taki: “Onmen beele u abi?” Ne den piki en taki: “Wi abi seibin beele.”
eng_text: He asked them, "How many loaves do you have?" They said, "Seven."

djk_text: Ne a taigi den sama taki: “U ala fiya sidon a doti.” Da ala den sama sidon enke fa Masaa Jesesi taki. Ne a teke den seibin beele, ne a gi Masaa Gadu daa moi, te a kaba. Ne a booko den beele pisipisi, ne a gi den bakaman fi en. Ne den teke den beele paati gi den sama.
eng_text: He commanded the multitude to sit down on the ground, and he took the seven loaves. Having given thanks, he broke them, and gave them to his disciples to serve, and they served the multitude.

djk_text: Da den be abi wantu fisi tu. Ne a teke den fisi, ne a gi Masaa Gadu daa. Ne a gi den bakaman fi en fu paati gi den sama tu.
eng_text: They had a few small fish. Having blessed them, he said to serve these also.

djk_text: Ne ala den sama nyan te den bee fuu. Da di den bakaman fu Masaa Jesesi piki san di den sama nyan fika, a fuu seibin bakisi.
eng_text: They ate, and were filled. They took up seven baskets of broken pieces that were left over.

djk_text: Da fu manengee wawan di nyan a doo fo dunsu. Da di den sama nyan kaba, ne Masaa Jesesi sende den fu den go a osu.
eng_text: Those who had eaten were about four thousand. Then he sent them away.

djk_text: Da fa i si a sende den sama gwe, ne en anga den bakaman fi en go a boto, ne den gwe a wan peesi den e kai Dalmanuta.
eng_text: Immediately he entered into the boat with his disciples, and came into the region of Dalmanutha.

djk_text: Da wantu Faliseiman be yee taki Masaa Jesesi be kon de. Ne den kon fu kon tesi en. Ne den bigin fu sitee anga Masaa Jesesi. Den sitee anga en te, ne den taigi en taki: “We, a bun. Da du wan foondoo sani, osi? Meke u si, da u sa biibi taki, na Masaa Gadu sende i kon a goontapu tuu.”
eng_text: The Pharisees came out and began to question him, seeking from him a sign from heaven, and testing him.

djk_text: Ne Masaa Jesesi dyeme, ne a akisi den taki: “Oho! Libisama! Saide meke u wani meke mi soi u maiki taki, na Masaa Gadu sende mi kon? Fu tuutuu mi ná o soi u ná wan maiki enke fa u wani de!”
eng_text: He sighed deeply in his spirit, and said, "Why does this generation seek a sign? Most certainly I tell you, no sign will be given to this generation."

djk_text: Ne a daai fesi, ne a waka go a ini wan boto, ne a koti go na abaase fika den taampu taampu de. Da den bakaman fi en be feegete fu bai nyanyan. Da den be abi wan kodo beele namo.
eng_text: He left them, and again entering into the boat, departed to the other side.

djk_text: Da di den be de a pasi e gwe, ne Masaa Jesesi be bali den taki: “U mu luku bun anga a sowda fu den Faliseiman anga di fu Kownu Helowdesi.”
eng_text: He warned them, saying, "Take heed: beware of the yeast of the Pharisees and the yeast of Herod."

djk_text: Da di Masaa Jesesi bali den so, ne den e akisi denseefi taki: “San a taki? San wani taki a sani di a taki de? Oo, a fu di u á bai beele meke a taki so.”
eng_text: They reasoned with one another, saying, "It's because we have no bread."

djk_text: Ma, da Masaa Jesesi be sabi taki na so den e taki. Ne a taigi den taki: “A ná fu di u á tyai beele meke mi taigi u a sani de. U á fusutan fa mi de ete, no? A so u don?
eng_text: Jesus, perceiving it, said to them, "Why do you reason that it's because you have no bread? Don't you perceive yet, neither understand? Is your heart still hardened?

djk_text: Luku onmen sani mi du di u si anga u ain anga onmen sani mi du di u yee anga u yesi. U feegete kaba,
eng_text: Having eyes, don't you see? Having ears, don't you hear? Don't you remember?

djk_text: fa mi be paati feifi beele gi feifi dunsu sama? Da onmen bakisi be de fanowdu fu u be poti san den sama be nyan fika?” Ne den piki en taki: “We, Masaa, na twalufu bakisi be fika.”
eng_text: When I broke the five loaves among the five thousand, how many baskets full of broken pieces did you take up?" They told him, "Twelve."

djk_text: Ne Masaa Jesesi akisi den baka taki: “Di mi be paati den seibin beele gi den fo dunsu sama, onmen bakisi be fika?” Ne den piki Masaa Jesesi taki: “Masaa, na seibin bakisi be fika.”
eng_text: When the seven loaves fed the four thousand, how many baskets full of broken pieces did you take up? They told him, "Seven."

djk_text: Ne Masaa Jesesi akisi den taki: “Da te enke now, u á fusutan mi ete, no?”
eng_text: He asked them, "Don't you understand, yet?"

djk_text: Da Masaa Jesesi anga den bakaman fi en doo wan peesi den e kai Betisaida. Ne den sama tyai wan beendiman kon ne en. Ne den begi en fu a sa langa ana oli a beendiman meke a si baka.
eng_text: He came to Bethsaida. They brought a blind man to him, and begged him to touch him.

djk_text: Ne Masaa Jesesi teke a man na ana tyai puu a pe somen sama be de. Ne a towe wataa mofu a ini a man ain, ne a poti ana ne en ain tapu. Ne a akisi en taki: “Yu e si sani kaba?”
eng_text: He took hold of the blind man by the hand, and brought him out of the village. When he had spit on his eyes, and laid his hands on him, he asked him if he saw anything.

djk_text: Ne a man luku lontu, ne a piki taki: “We, mi e si sama e waka. Ma a gei enke na udu bon e waka e lontu.”
eng_text: He looked up, and said, "I see men; for I see them like trees walking."

djk_text: Ne Masaa Jesesi poti ana ete wan leisi ne en ain tapu. Ne di Masaa Jesesi puu ana, ne a man luku peesi lontu baka. Ne en ain kiin kelle, ai si sani bun baka enke fa wan libisama mu si.
eng_text: Then again he laid his hands on his eyes. He looked intently, and was restored, and saw everyone clearly.

djk_text: Ne Masaa Jesesi sende a man taki: “Go a osu. Ma yu á mu go a ini a kondee go taigi sama taki na mi deesi yu.”
eng_text: He sent him away to his house, saying, "Don't enter into the village, nor tell anyone in the village."

djk_text: Ne moo lati, ne Masaa Jesesi anga den bakaman fi en go a den kondee kondee di de lontu Sesaleya Filipi. Da di den de a pasi e gwe di den waka doo wan pisi, ne Masaa Jesesi akisi den taki: “Sama den sama e taki mi de?”
eng_text: Jesus went out, with his disciples, into the villages of Caesarea Philippi. On the way he asked his disciples, "Who do men say that I am?"

djk_text: Ne den piki taki: “We, wantu taki yu na Johanisi a Dopuman. Taawan taki yu na Eliya, ofu wan fu den taa fositen apaiti takiman fu Masaa Gadu di weki komoto a dede baka.”
eng_text: They told him, "John the Baptizer, and others say Elijah, but others: one of the prophets."

djk_text: Da di den piki Masaa Jesesi so, ne a akisi den taki: “We u, no? Sama na mi?” Ne Peitilisi piki en taki: “Yu na a Kelestesi di Masaa Gadu sende kon!”
eng_text: He said to them, "But who do you say that I am?" Peter answered, "You are the Christ."

djk_text: Ne Masaa Jesesi bali den taanga taanga taki: “U á mu taigi ná wan sama, sama mi de!”
eng_text: He commanded them that they should tell no one about him.

djk_text: Da Masaa Jesesi bigin fu taigi den fu a gaan pina anga sitaafu di de fu kon ne en tapu. Ne a taigi den taki: “Den bigiman fu keliki anga den leliman fu Dyuweiti anga den gaansama fu kondee, o kai a Manpikin di saka kon toon libisama ya a kuutu. Da den o kii en. Ma te den kii en, da baka dii dei, da en o opo baka komoto a geebi.”
eng_text: He began to teach them that the Son of Man must suffer many things, and be rejected by the elders, the chief priests, and the scribes, and be killed, and after three days rise again.

djk_text: Da di a taigi den so, ne Peitilisi kai en go a wanse. Ne a kaasi en.
eng_text: He spoke to them openly. Peter took him, and began to rebuke him.

djk_text: Ma namo, Masaa Jesesi daai luku den taa bakaman fi en. Ne a bali Peitilisi taki: “Pasa komoto a mi baka ya! Yu didibii, saatan yu! Peitilisi! A sani di i taki de, á de enke fa Masaa Gadu e pakisei. I taki enke fa libisama e pakisei.”
eng_text: But he, turning around, and seeing his disciples, rebuked Peter, and said, "Get behind me, Satan! For you have in mind not the things of God, but the things of men."

djk_text: Ne Masaa Jesesi kai den taa bakaman fi en anga ala den sama di be kon makandii de kon moo koosube ne en. Ne a taigi den taki: “Efu wan sama wani waka a mi baka, da a á mu teli enseefi moo. Da a mu e tyai a sitaafu di o kon ne en tapu enke wan sama e tyai wan koloisi, fu den go sipikii en kii.
eng_text: He called the multitude to himself with his disciples, and said to them, "Whoever wants to come after me, let him deny himself, and take up his cross, and follow me.

djk_text: A sama di wani kibii en libi fu nyan fu a goontapu ya, sa lasi en libi. Ma a sama di ná abi toobi fu lasi en libi fu mi ede anga fu paati a Bun Nyunsu fu Masaa Gadu gi sama o libi tuutuu.
eng_text: For whoever wants to save his life will lose it; and whoever will lose his life for my sake and the sake of the Good News will save it.

djk_text: Da san i wini efi i nyan fu goontapu, gudu te a gudu, ma i lasi a libi fu tego go a didibii faya?
eng_text: For what does it profit a man, to gain the whole world, and forfeit his life?

djk_text: San i sa pai fi i fende i libi baka?
eng_text: For what will a man give in exchange for his life?

djk_text: Da fa u de a goontapu ya, da somen sama fika Masaa Gadu go e du ala sowtu ogii. Da efu wan sama e sen gi mi anga mi wowtu, da te a Manpikin di saka kon toon libisama ya o daai kon baka, da sen o kisi en fi en tu. Bika, a o kon anga den apaiti Basiya fu Masaa Gadu Kondee anga gaan dyendee fasi fu Masaa Gadu.”
eng_text: For whoever will be ashamed of me and of my words in this adulterous and sinful generation, the Son of Man also will be ashamed of him, when he comes in the glory of his Father with the holy angels."

djk_text: Ne Masaa Jesesi taigi den taki: “Mi e taigi u kiinkiin taki, son fu u di taampu ya ná o tesi dede, fosi u si a Nyun Tii fu Masaa Gadu kon doo anga ala a taanga fi en.”
eng_text: He said to them, "Most certainly I tell you, there are some standing here who will in no way taste death until they see the Kingdom of God come with power."

djk_text: Da baka sigisi dei, ne a teke Peitilisi anga Jakowbesi anga Johanisi tyai go a wan hei mongo. Da na den wawan be de ape. Namo di den de na a mongo ede, ne den si Masaa Jesesi fesi anga en hii sikin e beenki mala mala e koti faya gelen gelen.
eng_text: After six days Jesus took with him Peter, James, and John, and brought them up onto a high mountain privately by themselves, and he was changed into another form in front of them.

djk_text: En koosi weti fann. Da ná wan sama fu goontapu sa wasi en koosi kiin so.
eng_text: His clothing became glistening, exceedingly white, like snow, such as no launderer on earth can whiten them.

djk_text: Ne den si Eliya anga Mosesi kon na a mongo wanboo wanboo so. Ne den bigin taki anga Masaa Jesesi.
eng_text: Elijah and Moses appeared to them, and they were talking with Jesus.

djk_text: Ne Peitilisi taki: “Masaa! Meke u tan ya! Meke u meke dii pikin osu na a mongo ede ya. Wan fi yu. Wan fu Eliya anga wan fu Mosesi. Bika a switi fu toko fu u de makandii ya!”
eng_text: Peter answered Jesus, "Rabbi, it is good for us to be here. Let's make three tents: one for you, one for Moses, and one for Elijah."

djk_text: Da na a feele di Peitilisi feele namo, meke a taki den sani ya. Bika a á be sabi san a mu taki.
eng_text: For he didn't know what to say, for they were very afraid.

djk_text: Da te fu den poti pakisei, ne wanboo wanboo so wan woluku saka kon tapu den. Ne wan Tongo taki a ini a woluku ini taki: “Disi na mi Manpikin, di mi lobi tuutuu. U aliki ne en san ai taigi u.”
eng_text: A cloud came, overshadowing them, and a voice came out of the cloud, "This is my beloved Son. Listen to him."

djk_text: Ne di den luku baka, ne, woo! Den á si ná wan sama moo enke Masaa Jesesi wawan. Eliya anga Mosesi gwe.
eng_text: Suddenly looking around, they saw no one with them any more, except Jesus only.

djk_text: Ne di den e saka a mongo, ne Masaa Jesesi bali den taki: “U á mu taki san u si ya, ye! Ma, te a Manpikin di kon saka toon libisama a goontapu ya dede, te a opo baka a geebi, da u sa taki san u si ya.”
eng_text: As they were coming down from the mountain, he commanded them that they should tell no one what things they had seen, until after the Son of Man had risen from the dead.

djk_text: Da na so den dii man ya oli a toli ya fu denseefi. Ma den dii man e akisi denseefi taki: “San wani taki a o dede, da a opo baka komoto a geebi?”
eng_text: They kept this saying to themselves, questioning what the "rising from the dead" meant.

djk_text: Ne den akisi Masaa Jesesi taki: “Masaa Jesesi! Saide meke den leliman fu Dyuweiti e leli u taki, Eliya mu kon a goontapu fosi Masaa Gadu sende a Kelestesi kon?”
eng_text: They asked him, saying, "Why do the scribes say that Elijah must come first?"

djk_text: Ne Masaa Jesesi piki den taki: “We, na so a de tuu, taki Eliya mu kon fosi fu seeka sani bunbun fosi a Kelestesi sa kon. Ma Eliya kon kaba, te den du san den wani anga en enke fa den apaiti takiman fu Masaa Gadu be taki. Ma san den apaiti takiman fu Masaa Gadu be taki fu a Manpikin di saka kon toon libisama ya? San libisama o du anga en? Den apaiti takiman fu Gadu be taki kaba taki: ‘Den o pina en, si en enke soso wisiwasi sani.’ ”
eng_text: He said to them, "Elijah indeed comes first, and restores all things. How is it written about the Son of Man, that he should suffer many things and be despised?

djk_text: Di den kon doo a den taa bakaman fu Masaa Jesesi, ne den si den taa bakaman fu Masaa Jesesi anga somen sama. Da den anga wantu leliman fu Dyuweiti be e sitee anga denseefi.
eng_text: Coming to the disciples, he saw a great multitude around them, and scribes questioning them.

djk_text: Da, ne te fu den sama poti pakisei, ne Masaa Jesesi e kon. Da den be foondoo seefi. Ne den sama lon go gi en odi.
eng_text: Immediately all the multitude, when they saw him, were greatly amazed, and running to him greeted him.

djk_text: Ne a akisi den taki: “San pasa? San meke u e sitee ya so?”
eng_text: He asked the scribes, "What are you asking them?"

djk_text: Ne wan man piki Masaa Jesesi taki: “Masaa, yeepi mi! Mi tyai mi manpikin kon a yu. Wan takuu jeje de ne en tapu. Da a takuu jeje ya e tapu en mofu fu a á poi taki.
eng_text: One of the multitude answered, "Teacher, I brought to you my son, who has a mute spirit;

djk_text: Da alaten a takuu jeje kon ne en tapu, ai towe enseefi a doti e kaw tifi e puu sukuma a mofu fukuu. Da ai tiiki tiloo e taanga kwakwakwaa. Da di mi á be si yu, ne mi tyai en go gi den bakaman fi yu fu den puu a takuu jeje ne en tapu. Ma den á be poi puu en.”
eng_text: and wherever it seizes him, it throws him down, and he foams at the mouth, and grinds his teeth, and wastes away. I asked your disciples to cast it out, and they weren't able."

djk_text: Ne Masaa Jesesi bali gi den bakaman fi en anga den taa sama taki: “Oho! Libisama! Saide meke den libisama fu a ten ya nái biibi ete? On langa mi mu oli pasensi anga u ete fosi u kon biibi Gadu? U tyai a pikin kon.”
eng_text: He answered him, "Unbelieving generation, how long shall I be with you? How long shall I bear with you? Bring him to me."

djk_text: Ne den sama tyai a pikin kon gi Masaa Jesesi. Ne di a takuu jeje si Masaa Jesesi, ne a subi a boi te, en sikin taanga kwakwakwaa. Ne a towe en a doti, e lolo kungulun, kungulun. Sukuma e komoto ne en mofu.
eng_text: They brought him to him, and when he saw him, immediately the spirit convulsed him, and he fell on the ground, wallowing and foaming at the mouth.

djk_text: Ne Masaa Jesesi akisi a man taki: “On langa a pikin ya abi a siki ya kaba?” Ne a man piki taki: “Masaa! Na senten a de pikinengee.
eng_text: He asked his father, "How long has it been since this has come to him?" He said, "From childhood.

djk_text: Na onmen toon a takuu jeje towe en a ini faya anga wataa fu kii. Da gaantangi baa, Masaa, mi e begi yu, efi i poi yeepi mi!”
eng_text: Often it has cast him both into the fire and into the water, to destroy him. But if you can do anything, have compassion on us, and help us."

djk_text: Ne Masaa Jesesi piki a man taki: “I mu abi biibi a Gadu. Bika Masaa Gadu sa du ala sani gi wan sama di poti biibi ne en tapu.”
eng_text: Jesus said to him, "If you can believe, all things are possible to him who believes."

djk_text: Ne a man bali wanten taki: “Masaa! Masaa! Mi e biibi. Ma a biibi fu mi á sai. Ma gaantangi, yeepi mi meke mi sa biibi.”
eng_text: Immediately the father of the child cried out with tears, "I believe. Help my unbelief!"

djk_text: Di Masaa Jesesi luku, ne a si taki moo anga moo sama e kon. Ne fosi den doo, ne a kaasi a sani taki: “Komoto ne en tapu gwe wanten! Yu didibii di e tei en tongo e dofu en yesi fu a á yee sani! Komoto ne en tapu gwe! Da noiti moo i mu kon moo ne en tapu moo.”
eng_text: When Jesus saw that a multitude came running together, he rebuked the unclean spirit, saying to him, "You mute and deaf spirit, I command you, come out of him, and never enter him again!"

djk_text: Ne a takuu jeje kon na a pikin tapu moo taanga, ne a bali taanga, ne a gwe. Ne a pikin didon pii enke a dede. Ne den sama denki taki a pikin dede.
eng_text: Having cried out, and convulsed greatly, it came out of him. The boy became like one dead; so much that most of them said, "He is dead."

djk_text: Ma Masaa Jesesi oli en na ana, ne a opo en taampu. Ne a pikin taampu. A kon bun kelle.
eng_text: But Jesus took him by the hand, and raised him up; and he arose.

djk_text: Da pikin moo a baka Jesesi anga den bakaman fi en go a ini wan osu. Ne den bakaman fi en akisi en taki: “Masaa! Saide meke wi á be poi kaasi a takuu jeje puu na a pikin tapu?”
eng_text: When he had come into the house, his disciples asked him privately, "Why couldn't we cast it out?"

djk_text: Ne Masaa Jesesi piki den taki: “Den sowtu takuu jeje ya nái gwe efi i á de sondee nyan fu begi Masaa Gadu.”
eng_text: He said to them, "This kind can come out by nothing, except by prayer and fasting."

djk_text: Da Masaa Jesesi anga den bakaman fi en komoto na a kondee. Ne den waka go a Galileya. Da Masaa Jesesi á be wani sama sabi taki a be de ape.
eng_text: They went out from there, and passed through Galilee. He didn't want anyone to know it.

djk_text: Bika a be wani de anga den bakaman fi en wawan fu leli den. Ne a taigi den taki: “Den o seli a Manpikin di saka kon toon libisama ya, gi takuu ati sama fu kii. Da den o kii en. Ma baka dii dei a sa opo baka komoto a geebi.”
eng_text: For he was teaching his disciples, and said to them, "The Son of Man is being handed over to the hands of men, and they will kill him; and when he is killed, on the third day he will rise again."

djk_text: Da den bakaman fi en á be fusutan san a taigi den de. Ma anga ala fa den á fusutan san Masaa Jesesi taki de, toku ná wan fu den be abi a deki ati fu akisi en san wani taki a sani di a taki de.
eng_text: But they didn't understand the saying, and were afraid to ask him.

djk_text: Da di den doo Kafalnayemu, ne den go a ini wan osu. Ne Masaa Jesesi akisi den taki: “San u be e taki a pasi di u be e kon?”
eng_text: He came to Capernaum, and when he was in the house he asked them, "What were you arguing among yourselves on the way?"

djk_text: Ma den á be poi piki en, bika den be kuutu anga denseefi on di fu den na a moo heiwan fu den ala den.
eng_text: But they were silent, for they had disputed one with another on the way about who was the greatest.

djk_text: Ne Masaa Jesesi go sidon, ne a kai den kon. Ne a taigi den taki: “U aliki mi bun. Sama fu u di wani de a moo heiwan mu de a moo pikinwan a u mindii.”
eng_text: He sat down, and called the twelve; and he said to them, "If any man wants to be first, he shall be last of all, and servant of all."

djk_text: Ne a kai wan pikin kon ne en. Ne a pikin kon. Ne a lolo a pikin a neki, ne a taigi den taki:
eng_text: He took a little child, and set him in their midst. Taking him in his arms, he said to them,

djk_text: “Wan sama di lobi mi te a teke wan mofina sama enke a pikin totii pikin ya oli fu gaan sani fu di a de fu mi ede, da na mi a oli fu gaan sani. Da sama di oli mi fu gaan sani, oli mi Tata di sende mi kon fu gaan sani tu.”
eng_text: Whoever receives one such little child in my name, receives me, and whoever receives me, doesn't receive me, but him who sent me.

djk_text: Ne Johanisi taigi Masaa Jesesi taki: “Masaa, u miti wan man di teke i nen e puu takuu jeje a sama tapu. Ma u bali en taki a á mu teke i nen fu puu takuu jeje a sama tapu so. Bika en a ná wan bakaman fi yu enke wi.”
eng_text: John said to him, "Teacher, we saw someone who doesn't follow us casting out demons in your name; and we forbade him, because he doesn't follow us."

djk_text: Ma Masaa Jesesi piki den taki: “Nono! U be mu fika en. U á be mu tapu en. Bika wan sama di e teke mi nen e du foondoo sani, ná doo daai taki ogii fu mi esi esi.
eng_text: But Jesus said, "Don't forbid him, for there is no one who will do a mighty work in my name, and be able quickly to speak evil of me.

djk_text: Da soseefi tu, wan sama di nái libi ogii anga wi, na wan sama fu wi.” Ne Masaa Jesesi taigi den go doo taki:
eng_text: For whoever is not against us is on our side.

djk_text: “Mi e taigi u tuutuu taki: Efu wan sama gi u wan gaasi wataa fu di u de bakaman fu mi, da a sa kisi en paiman fu dati. U biibi san mi e taigi u ya. San a du gi u de ná abi lasi.”
eng_text: For whoever will give you a cup of water to drink in my name, because you are Christ's, most certainly I tell you, he will in no way lose his reward.

djk_text: Ne Masaa Jesesi taigi den bakaman fi en go doo taki: “I si fa a pikin de ya? Da efuso wan sama kon e biibi mi, ne i meke a du wan sani fu puu en a Masaa Gadu pasi, da na gaan ogii i du de. Da a moo betee i be meke den tei wan gaanbigi siton a i neki, da den iti i go a ini ze liba. Da mi e taigi u taki a sitaafu di yu o kisi o hebi seefi seefi.”
eng_text: Whoever will cause one of these little ones who believe in me to stumble, it would be better for him if he were thrown into the sea with a millstone hung around his neck.

djk_text: Ne a taigi den moo go doo taki: “Efu na i ana e koli yu fu meke i du ogii, da i mu koti en puu towe. Bika a moo bun i de anga wanse ana, da i go a Masaa Gadu Kondee pe dede á de moo. Moo enke i de anga tu ana, da i go a didibii faya di nái kaba boon.
eng_text: If your hand causes you to stumble, cut it off. It is better for you to enter into life maimed, rather than having your two hands to go into Gehenna, into the unquenchable fire,

djk_text: Da efu na i futu e koli yu fu meke i du ogii, da i mu koti en puu towe. Bika a moo bun i de anga wanse futu, da i kiipi go a Gadu Kondee pe libi ná a kaba ná wan ten. Moo enke i de anga tu se futu, da den iti yu go a didibii faya, te a yuu doo.
eng_text: If your foot causes you to stumble, cut it off. It is better for you to enter into life lame, rather than having your two feet to be cast into Gehenna, into the fire that will never be quenched--

djk_text: Da soseefi tu, efu na i ain e koli yu fu meke i du ogii, da i mu diki en puu towe. Bika a moo bun i de anga wanse ain, da i go a ini a Nyun Tii fu Masaa Gadu. Moo enke i de anga tu se ain, da den iti yu go a ini didibii faya.
eng_text: If your eye causes you to stumble, cast it out. It is better for you to enter into the Kingdom of God with one eye, rather than having two eyes to be cast into the Gehenna of fire,

djk_text: Da a pen fu a peesi de noiti abi kaba. Soseefi a faya noiti e tapu tu.”
eng_text: 'where their worm doesn't die, and the fire is not quenched.'

djk_text: Ne Masaa Jesesi taigi den baka taki: “We u luku! Sawtu na wan bun sani di e gi nyanyan tesi. Ma efu a lasi en kaakiti, da sani á de fu gi enmi en moo. Da na soseefi a libi fu u de. A mu abi kaakiti enke sawtu. Ma fosi a abi a kaakiti de, da u mu pasa a ini faya fosi. Ma efi i á pasa den somen sani de, da yu o de enke sawtu di lasi en kaakiti. Bika, ai yeepi wi fu a libi fu wi puu yeepi gi ala sama leti enke fa sawtu e gi nyanyan tesi. Da u mu libi fiifii anga useefi alaten.”
eng_text: For everyone will be salted with fire, and every sacrifice will be seasoned with salt.

djk_text: Ne Masaa Jesesi komoto ape, ne a go na a pisi fu Judeja na abaase fu a Joodani Liba. Da somen sama be kon ne en. Ne a bigin fu leli den enke fa a be gwenti.
eng_text: He arose from there and came into the borders of Judea and beyond the Jordan. Multitudes came together to him again. As he usually did, he was again teaching them.

djk_text: Da, ne wan duupu Faliseiman kon ne en. Da na kon den be kon tesi en. Di den doo, ne den akisi en taki: “Masaa, efu wan man anga wan uman libi, a bun fu a man fika a uman moo? San a weiti fu Gadu taigi u fu dati?”
eng_text: Pharisees came to him testing him, and asked him, "Is it lawful for a man to divorce his wife?"

djk_text: Ne Masaa Jesesi akisi den taki: “San a weiti di Mosesi sikiifi fika gi u e soi wi?”
eng_text: He answered, "What did Moses command you?"

djk_text: Ne den piki Masaa Jesesi taki: “Ya! A weiti fu Mosesi e soi wi taki, efu wan man wani, a sa paati anga en uman. Ma, da a mu meke wan pampila gi a uman taki en anga en á de moo. Da te a meke a pampila ya so, da a sa sende en gwe.”
eng_text: They said, "Moses allowed a certificate of divorce to be written, and to divorce her."

djk_text: Ne Masaa Jesesi piki den taki: “Na tuu san u taki. Ma u sabi fu san ede meke Mosesi be sikiifi a weiti ya fika gi u? Na fu di u ati taanga. U nái yee sani fu du san Masaa Gadu wani.
eng_text: But Jesus said to them, "For your hardness of heart, he wrote you this commandment.

djk_text: Ma fosifosi, di Masaa Gadu be meke goontapu, da a be meke wan uman anga wan man.
eng_text: But from the beginning of the creation, God made them male and female.

djk_text: A dati meke, wan man e fika en gaansama osu, fu go teke en uman libi.
eng_text: For this cause a man will leave his father and mother, and will join to his wife,

djk_text: Da den tu sama de mokisa libi toon wan sikin. Da den nái teli fu tu sama moo, ma na wan sikin namo.
eng_text: and the two will become one flesh, so that they are no longer two, but one flesh.

djk_text: Da ná wan sama mu paati san di Masaa Gadu meke toon wan.”
eng_text: What therefore God has joined together, let no man separate."

djk_text: Ne di Masaa Jesesi kaba taki so, ne en anga den bakaman fi en go a osu baka. Ne di den de a osu de, ne den akisi en taki: “Masaa! San wani taki a sani di i taigi den sama de?” Ne Masaa Jesesi piki den taki:
eng_text: In the house, his disciples asked him again about the same matter.

djk_text: “Efu wan man towe en uman fu go libi anga wan taa uman, da a kai a motyo libi.
eng_text: He said to them, "Whoever divorces his wife, and marries another, commits adultery against her.

djk_text: Da soseefi, efu wan uman towe en man fu go libi anga wan taa man, da a kai a motyo libi.”
eng_text: If a woman herself divorces her husband, and marries another, she commits adultery."

djk_text: Da wantu sama be tyai den pikin kon a Masaa Jesesi, fu a be poti ana a den pikin tapu, begi Masaa Gadu gi den. Ma den bakaman fi en bali den, fu den á tyai den pikin kon a Masaa Jesesi.
eng_text: They were bringing to him little children, that he should touch them, but the disciples rebuked those who were bringing them.

djk_text: Ma namo, Masaa Jesesi si, ne a mandii a den bakaman fi en. Ne a bali den taki: “U fika den pikin, meke denseefi kon doo a mi tu. U á tapu den! Bika na sama di abi a fasi di pikinengee abi sa poi go doo a ini a Nyun Tii a Masaa Gadu Kondee.
eng_text: But when Jesus saw it, he was moved with indignation, and said to them, "Allow the little children to come to me! Don't forbid them, for the Kingdom of God belongs to such as these.

djk_text: Da efu wan sama nái biibi Masaa Gadu enke fa wan pikinengee e biibi sani, da a ná o poi doo a ini a Nyun Tii fu Masaa Gadu.”
eng_text: Most certainly I tell you, whoever will not receive the Kingdom of God like a little child, he will in no way enter into it."

djk_text: Ne a teke den pikinengee wai kon ne en, ne a poti ana a den ede, ne a begi gi den.
eng_text: He took them in his arms, and blessed them, laying his hands on them.

djk_text: Namo, ne di Masaa Jesesi de a pasi e gwe, ne wan yonkuman lon kon ne en. Ne a sutu kini a doti, ne a bali taki: “Mi bun Masaa! San mi mu du fu mi fende a libi fu ten fu ten?”
eng_text: As he was going out into the way, one ran to him, knelt before him, and asked him, "Good Teacher, what shall I do that I may inherit eternal life?"

djk_text: Ne Masaa Jesesi piki en taki: “Saide meke yu e kai mi bun Masaa? Ma i sabi san yu e taki di yu e kai mi bun Masaa? A ná Masaa Gadu wawan bun, no? Da i sabi den weiti di Masaa Gadu poti gi den sama kaba. Dati na: ‘I á mu kii sama. I á mu waka anga taa uman ofu man. Da soseefi, i á mu fufuu, i á mu lei, i á mu koli sama nyan a den sikin. Da i mu lesipeki i mma anga i dda.’ ”
eng_text: Jesus said to him, "Why do you call me good? No one is good except one--God.

djk_text: Ne a man piki Masaa Jesesi taki: “We, Masaa! Senten mi de pikinengee, mi e oli ala den weiti de te enke tide.”
eng_text: He said to him, "Teacher, I have observed all these things from my youth."

djk_text: Ne Masaa Jesesi luku en dunn, ne tyali fu a man kisi Masaa Jesesi. Ne a taigi en taki: “Man, wan sani de di i mankei ete. Go a osu, da seli ala san yu abi, da paati a moni gi den pootiman, da i sa gudu a Gadu Kondee a tapu. Da te i seli den kaba, da kon baka fu toon wan bakaman fu mi.”
eng_text: Jesus looking at him loved him, and said to him, "One thing you lack. Go, sell whatever you have, and give to the poor, and you will have treasure in heaven; and come, follow me, taking up the cross."

djk_text: Ne a man kwinsi en fesi, ne a waka gwe anga gaanbigi tyali a ini en ati, bika a man ya be gudu tuutuu.
eng_text: But his face fell at that saying, and he went away sorrowful, for he was one who had great possessions.

djk_text: Ne Masaa Jesesi daai, ne a taigi den bakaman fi en taki: “U si fa a taanga gi wan guduman fu a kon a ini a Nyun Tii fu Masaa Gadu?”
eng_text: Jesus looked around, and said to his disciples, "How difficult it is for those who have riches to enter into the Kingdom of God!"

djk_text: Da den bakaman fu Masaa Jesesi be foondoo seefi seefi. Ma Masaa Jesesi taigi den taki: “Eeye! A taanga seefi seefi gi wan guduman fu kon a ini a Nyun Tii fu Masaa Gadu.
eng_text: The disciples were amazed at his words. But Jesus answered again, "Children, how hard is it for those who trust in riches to enter into the Kingdom of God!

djk_text: A taanga gi wan kameili fu waka pasa a wan nanai olo. Ma mi e taigi u taki, a moo taanga gi wan guduman fu a pasa kon a ini a Nyun Tii fu Masaa Gadu.”
eng_text: It is easier for a camel to go through a needle's eye than for a rich man to enter into the Kingdom of God."

djk_text: Da a sani di a taki ya be dangaa den bakaman fi en seefi seefi. Ne den akisi en taki: “Da sama o poi go a Nyun Tii fu Masaa Gadu seefi?”
eng_text: They were exceedingly astonished, saying to him, "Then who can be saved?"

djk_text: Ne Masaa Jesesi luku den, ne a taigi den taki: “Efu u luku a libisama fasi, da ná wan sama o poi go. Ma Masaa Gadu e poi du ala sani.”
eng_text: Jesus, looking at them, said, "With men it is impossible, but not with God, for all things are possible with God."

djk_text: Ne Peitilisi piki taki: “We, Masaa, u no? U fika ala sani fu waka a yu baka e go anga yu na ala peesi!”
eng_text: Peter began to tell him, "Behold, we have left all, and have followed you."

djk_text: Ne Masaa Jesesi piki en taki: “Iniiwan sama di lobi mi te, a fika en osu efu en baala efu en sisa efu en dda efu en mma ofu pikin efu ala san a abi, fu a Bun Nyunsu ede.
eng_text: Jesus said, "Most certainly I tell you, there is no one who has left house, or brothers, or sisters, or father, or mother, or wife, or children, or land, for my sake, and for the sake of the Good News,

djk_text: Da so wan sama o fende wan ondoo toon nownow fu san a fika fu kon waka a mi baka a goontapu ya, efu na osu, baala, mma, pikin anga gudu. Ma sama o de di o go e pina den fu mi ede tu. Da den o fende a libi fu tego a Masaa Gadu a bakaten tu.
eng_text: but he will receive one hundred times more now in this time, houses, brothers, sisters, mothers, children, and land, with persecutions; and in the age to come eternal life.

djk_text: Da na a seefi ten ya, da somen fesiwan ya o toon bakaman. Da somen di de bakaman ya o daai toon fesiwan.”
eng_text: But many who are first will be last; and the last first."

djk_text: Da den de a pasi e go a Jelusalem Foto. Da Masaa Jesesi be e waka a den fesi. Da den bakaman fi en anga den sama di be e waka anga den be e tan so feele feele. Di den waka te wan pisi, ne Masaa Jesesi kai den twalufu bakaman fi en go a wanse fu taigi den san o pasa anga en.
eng_text: They were on the way, going up to Jerusalem; and Jesus was going in front of them, and they were amazed; and those who followed were afraid. He again took the twelve, and began to tell them the things that were going to happen to him.

djk_text: Ne a taigi den taki: “U si fa wi e go a Jelusalem ya, den o seli a Manpikin di kon saka toon libisama ya, poti a ini a ana fu den bigiman fu keliki anga den leliman fu Dyuweiti. Da den o tyai en go a kuutu. Da den o fiti mofu fu kii en. Da den o poti en na ini ana fu den Loma sama di e tii a kondee ya.
eng_text:
Behold, we are going up to Jerusalem. The Son of Man will be delivered to the chief priests and the scribes. They will condemn him to death, and will deliver him to the Gentiles.
1460	Da den sama de o meke sipowtu anga en lafu en. Den o towe wataa mofu a ini en fesi. Den o wipi en wan mesaandi wipi fosi, da den tyai en go kii. Ma baka dii dei te a dede, da a o opo komoto baka a dede.”	1460	They will mock him, spit on him, scourge him, and kill him. On the third day he will rise again.

djk_text: Da di den e waka, ne den tu manpikin fu Da Sebedi di den e kai Jakowbesi anga Johanisi akisi en taki: “Masaa, u wani begi i wan sani baa. U wani begi yu fi i du wan sani gi u.”
eng_text: James and John, the sons of Zebedee, came near to him, saying, "Teacher, we want you to do for us whatever we will ask."

djk_text: Ne Masaa Jesesi akisi den taki: “San u wani begi mi?”
eng_text: He said to them, "What do you want me to do for you?"

djk_text: Ne den akisi en taki: “Masaa, na a ten di de a u fesi e kon te i sa ligei anga gaan lesipeki anga kaakiti, da meke u tu man ya sidon a yu se. Wan a yu leti ana se anga wan a yu kukutu ana se.”
eng_text: They said to him, "Grant to us that we may sit, one at your right hand, and one at your left hand, in your glory."

djk_text: Ne Masaa Jesesi piki den taki: “U sabi san u e akisi de? A gaan sitaafu anga pina di de fu kon a mi tapu u o poi tyai en? Na a ten di de a u fesi e kon, a gei enke mi o diingi wan gaan bita diingi a ini wan kan. Da u o poi diingi en?”
eng_text: But Jesus said to them, "You don't know what you are asking. Are you able to drink the cup that I drink, and to be baptized with the baptism that I am baptized with?"

djk_text: Ne den piki Masaa Jesesi taki: “Iya! U o poi diingi en.” Ne Masaa Jesesi piki den taki: “U sa diingi en tuu. Ma a pina di de fu kon a mi tapu o kon a u tapu tu. San o pasa anga mi o pasa anga u tu.
eng_text: They said to him, "We are able." Jesus said to them, "You shall indeed drink the cup that I drink, and you shall be baptized with the baptism that I am baptized with;

djk_text: Ma a á didon a mi fu taki sama sidon a mi kukutu ana efu mi leti ana. Na Masaa Gadu seefi e seeka peesi gi sama.”
eng_text: but to sit at my right hand and at my left hand is not mine to give, but for whom it has been prepared."

djk_text: Da di den taa tin bakaman fu Masaa Jesesi yee taki Jakowbesi anga Johanisi akisi Masaa Jesesi fu so wan hei peesi, ne den ati boon seefi seefi.
eng_text: When the ten heard it, they began to be indignant towards James and John.

djk_text: Da Masaa Jesesi kai den kon ne en. Ne a taigi den taki: “Den edeman fu kondee lobi taki a sama tapu. Den lobi dwengi sama, fu den du san den wani.
eng_text: Jesus summoned them, and said to them, "You know that they who are recognized as rulers over the nations lord it over them, and their great ones exercise authority over them.

djk_text: Ma u á de enke den sama ya. U de taa fasi. Da u mu libi taa fasi tu. Efu wan sama wani de moo hei moo den taawan, da a mu saka enseefi fu e dini den taawan.
eng_text: But it shall not be so among you, but whoever wants to become great among you shall be your servant.

djk_text: Da efu wan fu u wani de a fesi fu den taawan, da a mu toon saafu gi den taawan.
eng_text: Whoever of you wants to become first among you, shall be bondservant of all.
