eng_text: After these things the Lord appointed other seventy also, and sent them two and two before his face into every city and place, whither he himself would come.

djk_text: Ne a taigi den taki: “Sama de ipi a den peesi peesi di wani yee a Bun Nyunsu fu Masaa Gadu, fu den du san ai taki. Ma wookoman ná ipi sai fu go paati en. U begi Masaa Gadu di de basi fu a wooko, fu a puu moo wookoman sende go a ini a wooko fi en.
eng_text: Therefore said he unto them, The harvest truly is great, but the labourers are few: pray ye therefore the Lord of the harvest, that he would send forth labourers into his harvest.

djk_text: U go! Mi e sende u go enke te mi be o sende sikapu go a mindii fu takuu meti.
eng_text: Go your ways: behold, I send you forth as lambs among wolves.

djk_text: Ma te u e go, u á mu tyai moni, u á mu tyai saka. Da anga den susu di de a u futu de namo u mu go. U á mu tyai taawan moo enke di u wei de. U á mu tapu a pasi e taki gaan langa bee toli anga sama.
eng_text: Carry neither purse, nor scrip, nor shoes: and salute no man by the way.

djk_text: “Da ala osu ini di u o go, da u mu begi gi den sama taki: ‘Meke Masaa Gadu de anga den.’
eng_text: And into whatsoever house ye enter, first say, Peace be to this house.

djk_text: Da efu wan sama de ape di fiti fu kisi a bun di i begi gi en ya, da a bun o tan a ini a osu de. Ma efu a sama de á fiti fu kisi a bun ya, da a bun fi yu o daai kon a yu baka.
eng_text: And if the son of peace be there, your peace shall rest upon it: if not, it shall turn to you again.

djk_text: Ma te den teke u oli a wan osu, da na a osu de namo u mu tan. U á mu komoto fu awan osu go na a taawan. Te den gi u sani fu nyan, da u mu nyan. U á mu meke sen kisi u. Bika wan wookoman fiti fu kisi a paiman fu a wooko di ai du.
eng_text: And in the same house remain, eating and drinking such things as they give: for the labourer is worthy of his hire. Go not from house to house.

djk_text: “Da te u doo wan kondee, ne den kai u kon, da na san di den poti gi u fu nyan, na dati u mu nyan.
eng_text: And into whatsoever city ye enter, and they receive you, eat such things as are set before you:

djk_text: U deesi den sikiman di de ape. Da u taigi den sama taki: ‘A Nyun Tii fu Masaa Gadu kon koosube fu u.’
eng_text: And heal the sick that are therein, and say unto them, The kingdom of God is come nigh unto you.

djk_text: Ma, efu u doo a wan kondee, ne den sama á wani yee u taki, da u mu go taampu a mindii ganda, da u bali taigi den taki:
eng_text: But into whatsoever city ye enter, and they receive you not, go your ways out into the streets of the same, and say,

djk_text: ‘U luku ya! Disi na a santi fu a kondee, wi e sibi puu a u futu towe fika ya gi u. Da na wan maiki fu soi taki, u be taigi u a Bun Nyunsu. Da di Masaa Gadu o sitaafu u, da a ná wi fowtu. Bika u be taigi u fu a Nyun Tii fi en, ma u á be wani aliki wi. Kwolon! U e gwe, ye!’ ”
eng_text: Even the very dust of your city, which cleaveth on us, we do wipe off against you: notwithstanding be ye sure of this, that the kingdom of God is come nigh unto you.

djk_text: Ne Masaa Jesesi taigi den bakaman fi en go doo taki: “U mu de sabi sabi taki, na a gaanbigi dei di Masaa Gadu o kuutu goontapu, da a sitaafu di Masaa Gadu o sitaafu den sama fu a kondee de, o ogii moo enke a sitaafu di a be sitaafu a kondee di den e kai Sowdom.”
eng_text: But I say unto you, that it shall be more tolerable in that day for Sodom, than for that city.

djk_text: “Ma heelu fu den sama fu Kolasin anga Betisaida Foto! Bika efu den sama fu den takuu foto di den e kai Sidon anga Tilosi be si den gaan foondoo sani di mi du a u mindii ya, da gaandiwe den be o daai den libi. Bika na buduufu buduufu den be o de, fu a takuu libi fu den. Da den be o wei boko koosi a sikin, go sidon a doti e iti asisi a den sikin.
eng_text: Woe unto thee, Chorazin! woe unto thee, Bethsaida! for if the mighty works had been done in Tyre and Sidon, which have been done in you, they had a great while ago repented, sitting in sackcloth and ashes.

djk_text: A dati, meke a dei di Masaa Gadu o kuutu goontapu, Kolasin anga Betisaida Foto o kisi moo gaan sitaafu moo den.
eng_text: But it shall be more tolerable for Tyre and Sidon at the judgment, than for you.

djk_text: Da u fu Kafalnayemu Foto. San u e denki? U denki taki, a hei fu u o tyai u go a Masaa Gadu? Nono! A ná o tyai u go a Masaa Gadu. A didibii faya a o tyai u go.”
eng_text: And thou, Capernaum, which art exalted to heaven, shalt be thrust down to hell.

djk_text: Ne a taigi den bakaman fi en taki: “Efu wan sama e teke san u e taki, da ai teke san mi e taki tu. Ma, efu wan sama nái aliki u, san u e taki, da a nái aliki mi tu. Da sama di nái aliki mi, da a nái aliki Masaa Gadu, di sende mi kon tu.”
eng_text: He that heareth you heareth me; and he that despiseth you despiseth me; and he that despiseth me despiseth him that sent me.

djk_text: Ne baka wan pisiten, ne den seibintenti a tu bakaman fu Masaa Jesesi di a be sende gwe, daai kon ne en baka anga gaan piisii. Den taigi en taki: “Masaa! Di u teke a nen fi yu kaasi den takuu jeje, da den e du san u taki.”
eng_text: And the seventy returned again with joy, saying, Lord, even the devils are subject unto us through thy name.

djk_text: Ne Masaa Jesesi piki den taki: “Miseefi be si fa didibii makiti booko langa ten kaba. Mi si a komoto a tapu nyaw kai kon a doti, enke te donduu e koti faya.
eng_text: And he said unto them, I beheld Satan as lightning fall from heaven.

djk_text: We, mi gi u makiti a tapu fu ala wooko fu a feyanti. Soseefi mi gi u makiti a tapu fu sineki anga kukutu tee anga ala taa sani di a feyanti o wani sende kon, fu du ogii anga u. Da fu tuu, ná wan o poi du u ogii.
eng_text: Behold, I give unto you power to tread on serpents and scorpions, and over all the power of the enemy: and nothing shall by any means hurt you.

djk_text: Ma u á mu piisii, fu di den takuu jeje e du san u taki. Nono! Ma u mu piisii fu di u sabi taki, u nen sikiifi a Masaa Gadu.”
eng_text: Notwithstanding in this rejoice not, that the spirits are subject unto you; but rather rejoice, because your names are written in heaven.

djk_text: Ne a Apaiti Jeje fu Masaa Gadu fuu Masaa Jesesi ati anga gaan piisii. Ne a taki: “Mi Tata! Masaa fu tapu anga goontapu. Mi e gi yu gaantangi, fu di yu kibii den sani ya, gi den koniman anga den leliman fu a goontapu ya, te den á poi sabi den. Ma i meke den mofina sama ya kon sabi den. Ai baa, mi Tata! Gaantangi fi i. Bika na so i si taki a bun.”
eng_text: In that hour Jesus rejoiced in spirit, and said, I thank thee, O Father, Lord of heaven and earth, that thou hast hid these things from the wise and prudent, and hast revealed them unto babes: even so, Father; for so it seemed good in thy sight.

djk_text: Ne Masaa Jesesi taigi den sama taki: “Mi Tata poti ala sani a ini mi ana. Da ná wan sama kaba sabi a Pikin, boiti a Tata. Soseefi ná wan sama sabi a Tata, boiti a Pikin anga den sama di a Pikin wani meke kon sabi en.”
eng_text: All things are delivered to me of my Father: and no man knoweth who the Son is, but the Father; and who the Father is, but the Son, and he to whom the Son will reveal him.

djk_text: Ne Masaa Jesesi daai luku den bakaman fi en, ne a taigi den taki: “Seigi fu u, fu den sani di u e si anga den di u e yee ya.
eng_text: And he turned him unto his disciples, and said privately, Blessed are the eyes which see the things that ye see:

djk_text: Bika somen apaiti takiman fu Masaa Gadu anga kownu fu fesiten be angii fu si den sani di u e si ya. Ma den á be si den. Soseefi den be angii fu yee san u e yee ya, ma den á be yee den.”
eng_text: For I tell you, that many prophets and kings have desired to see those things which ye see, and have not seen them; and to hear those things which ye hear, and have not heard them.

djk_text: Ma namo, da wan dei, ne wan leliman fu Dyuweiti go a Masaa Jesesi go tesi en. Ne a akisi en taki: “Mesiti, oo! San mi mu du, fu mi fende a libi, fu ten fu ten a Masaa Gadu?”
eng_text: And, behold, a certain lawyer stood up, and tempted him, saying, Master, what shall I do to inherit eternal life?

djk_text: Ne Masaa Jesesi akisi en taki: “San sikiifi a Masaa Gadu Buku? San yu e leisi ne en?”
eng_text: He said unto him, What is written in the law? how readest thou?

djk_text: Ne a piki en taki: “We, a sikiifi taki: ‘I mu lobi Masaa Gadu anga yu hiihii ati anga i hii fii anga hii i taanga anga hii i fusutan. Da i mu lobi taawan a i se leti enke fa i lobi iseefi.’ ”
eng_text: And he answering said, Thou shalt love the Lord thy God with all thy heart, and with all thy soul, and with all thy strength, and with all thy mind; and thy neighbour as thyself.

djk_text: Ne Masaa Jesesi piki en taki: “Na so a de! I piki bun. Libi pilisisi enke fa i taki de, da yu o fende a libi fu tego.”
eng_text: And he said unto him, Thou hast answered right: this do, and thou shalt live.

djk_text: We, di a man si taki, Masaa Jesesi á piki en enke fa a be wani, ne a daai, ne a akisi Masaa Jesesi baka taki: “Ma sama na den taa sama, di mi mu lobi enke miseefi?”
eng_text: But he, willing to justify himself, said unto Jesus, And who is my neighbour?

djk_text: Ne Masaa Jesesi gi en wan ageisi toli taki: “Wan man be komoto a Jelusalem Foto e saka go a Jelikow Foto. Da di ai gwe te wan pisi, ne fufuuman feti anga en. Ne den fonmi en te, a fon, teke den koosi ne en sikin anga ala san a be tyai. Ne den fika en de swaki a sikin pasi. Ne den gwe fu den.
eng_text: And Jesus answering said, A certain man went down from Jerusalem to Jericho, and fell among thieves, which stripped him of his raiment, and wounded him, and departed, leaving him half dead.

djk_text: Ne te wan pisi, ne wan apaiti begiman fu keliki e kon pasa. Ma di a si a man a doti, ne a koti lontu, waka pasa fi en a taase.
eng_text: And by chance there came down a certain priest that way: and when he saw him, he passed by on the other side.

djk_text: Te wan pisi baka, ne wan man fu Leifi Lo, di e wooko a ini a Mama Keliki e kon pasa. Ne di a si a man, ne a luku en dunn, ne enseefi koti lontu waka pasa gwe fi en.
eng_text: And likewise a Levite, when he was at the place, came and looked on him, and passed by on the other side.

djk_text: “Ne bakadati, ne wan Samaliya sama e kon pasa de tu. Ne di a si a man a doti de, ne gaan tyali fu a man kisi en te, ná sipowtu.
eng_text: But a certain Samaritan, as he journeyed, came where he was: and when he saw him, he had compassion on him,

djk_text: Ne a go, ne a bendi kiin den soo fi en, lobi deesi gi den, tei den moi, te a kaba. Ne a opo en poti na a buliki fi en tapu, ne a lei anga en, te a wan lanti osu. Ne a seeka en baka, te a kaba.
eng_text: And went to him, and bound up his wounds, pouring in oil and wine, and set him on his own beast, and brought him to an inn, and took care of him.

djk_text: Ne a taa dei, ne a teke moni, ne a gi a man di abi a lanti osu taki: ‘Luku ya! Gaantangi! Luku a man ya bun gi mi, baa? Da efu a moni á sai, da te mi e daai, da mi sa pai yu doo.’ ”
eng_text: And on the morrow when he departed, he took out two pence, and gave them to the host, and said unto him, Take care of him; and whatsoever thou spendest more, when I come again, I will repay thee.

djk_text: We, ne Masaa Jesesi akisi a man taki: “On di fu den dii man ya, i denki libi anga en enke a taawan ne en se, di a mu lobi enke enseefi?”
eng_text: Which now of these three, thinkest thou, was neighbour unto him that fell among the thieves?

djk_text: Ne a man taki: “Na a man di be abi tyali ati fi en!” Ne Masaa Jesesi piki en taki: “Weeno! Na so a de enke fa i piki de tuu. Go, da i libi enke fa a man ya libi.”
eng_text: And he said, He that shewed mercy on him. Then said Jesus unto him, Go, and do thou likewise.

djk_text: Da, di Masaa Jesesi anga den bakaman fi en de a pasi e go a Jelusalem, ne den doo wan kondee pe wan uman den kai Malita e tan. Ne a kai Masaa Jesesi anga den bakaman fi en, fu den go ne en osu. Ne den go.
eng_text: Now it came to pass, as they went, that he entered into a certain village: and a certain woman named Martha received him into her house.

djk_text: Da Malita be abi wan sisa den e kai Maliya. Da fanafu di Masaa Jesesi go a ini a osu, ne Maliya go sidon te ne en ini, e aliki san ai taki.
eng_text: And she had a sister called Mary, which also sat at Jesus' feet, and heard his word.

djk_text: Ma Malita be e booko ede e seeka nyanyan gi Masaa Jesesi anga den bakaman fi en. Ne di Malita wooko te wan pisi, ne a á poi teke en moo. Bika a wooko kon hebi gi en. Ne a go a Masaa Jesesi taki: “Masaa! Yu nái si, no? Fu senten di i kon ya, ne Maliya go sidon fika a wooko gi mi wawan. Yu á poi sende en fu a kon yeepi mi, no?”
eng_text: But Martha was cumbered about much serving, and came to him, and said, Lord, dost thou not care that my sister hath left me to serve alone? bid her therefore that she help me.

djk_text: Ne Masaa Jesesi piki en taki: “Kee! Malita! Saide meke yu e booko yu ede a somen sani so?
eng_text: And Jesus answered and said unto her, Martha, Martha, thou art careful and troubled about many things:

djk_text: Na wankodo sani namo de di yu abi fanowdu. Maliya du a moo bun sani. Da mi ná o puu en ne en.”
eng_text: But one thing is needful: and Mary hath chosen that good part, which shall not be taken away from her.

djk_text: Ma namo, da wan dei, da Masaa Jesesi go a wan peesi go e begi. Di a begi te a kaba, ne wan fu den bakaman fi en kon ne en taki: “Masaa! Leli u begi tu, enke fa Johanisi be leli den bakaman fi en.”
eng_text: And it came to pass, that, as he was praying in a certain place, when he ceased, one of his disciples said unto him, Lord, teach us to pray, as John also taught his disciples.

djk_text: Ne a piki den taki: “Te u e begi, da u begi so: ‘Kee! Wi Tata! Meke ala sani sa kon lesipeki yu nen, wan apaiti fasi. Meke a Nyun Tii fi yu sa paati a hii goontapu.
eng_text: And he said unto them, When ye pray, say, Our Father which art in heaven, Hallowed be thy name. Thy kingdom come. Thy will be done, as in heaven, so in earth.

djk_text: Wi e begi yu, fu gi wi san wi abi fanowdu, fu nyan ibii dei baka.
eng_text: Give us day by day our daily bread.

djk_text: Gi wi paadon fu takuudu anga ogii di wi e du a yu fesi, leti enke fa wiseefi e gi taawan di e du ogii anga wi paadon. Wi e begi yu, fu kibii wi, meke wi á kai a ini tesi.’ ”
eng_text: And forgive us our sins; for we also forgive every one that is indebted to us. And lead us not into temptation; but deliver us from evil.

djk_text: Ne a taigi den go doo taki: “Meke u taki, yu abi wan bun mati, ne i go ne en a mindii neti, fu go yuu dii beele.
eng_text: And he said unto them, Which of you shall have a friend, and shall go unto him at midnight, and say unto him, Friend, lend me three loaves;

djk_text: Da yu o go weki en, da i taigi en taki: ‘Mati, gaantangi baa! Mi kon begi i wan sani. Wan mati fu mi komoto a wan faawe peesi kon a mi. Ma mi ná abi ná wan sani fu gi en, fu a nyan.’
eng_text: For a friend of mine in his journey is come to me, and I have nothing to set before him?

djk_text: Da, meke u taki a mati fi yu piki i taki: ‘Mi ná o poi opo go teke beele gi i moo. Mi anga den pikin sooto doo go didon kaba. Da fika mi, meke mi siibi fu mi.’ Ma fu di a fuka fi i bigi, meke i o go e naki a doo, e begi en naamo.
eng_text: And he from within shall answer and say, Trouble me not: the door is now shut, and my children are with me in bed; I cannot rise and give thee.

djk_text: Ma ná fu di yu anga en na mati ede, meke a o opo a doo gi yu. Ma na fu di i tan e naki a doo naamo, te a á poi fende pasi fu siibi, meke a musu opo go teke a beele di yu abi fanowdu gi yu.
eng_text: I say unto you, Though he will not rise and give him, because he is his friend, yet because of his importunity he will rise and give him as many as he needeth.

djk_text: “Na dati ede meke mi taigi u taki: ‘Begi, da u o kisi. U suku, da u o fende. U koko, da doo o opo gi u.’
eng_text: And I say unto you, Ask, and it shall be given you; seek, and ye shall find; knock, and it shall be opened unto you.

djk_text: Bika na sama di e begi en, e kisi. A sama di e suku e fende. Soseefi sama di e koko, da doo e opo gi.
eng_text: For every one that asketh receiveth; and he that seeketh findeth; and to him that knocketh it shall be opened.

djk_text: “Bika luku son fu u ya abi pikin. Da efu wan pikin fu u begi u wan fisi, u o teke wan sineki, da u gi en?
eng_text: If a son shall ask bread of any of you that is a father, will he give him a stone? or if he ask a fish, will he for a fish give him a serpent?

djk_text: Ofu, sama fu u di de ya, o teke wan kukutu tee langa gi en pikin, te a begi en wan igi?
eng_text: Or if he shall ask an egg, will he offer him a scorpion?

djk_text: We, efu anga ala fa u de takuu ati sama seefi, ne u sabi fu gi u pikin bun so, da san na u Tata a tapu? Te u begi en, a Apaiti Jeje fi en, a ná o gi u en moo esi, no?”
eng_text: If ye then, being evil, know how to give good gifts unto your children: how much more shall your heavenly Father give the Holy Spirit to them that ask him?

djk_text: Da wan taa dei baka, ne Masaa Jesesi yaki wan takuu jeje puu a wan sama tapu. A takuu jeje ya be meke a toon babawman. Ma wanten, di Masaa Jesesi yaki en puu, ne a man e taki bun baka. Da a sani foondoo ala den sama.
eng_text: And he was casting out a devil, and it was dumb. And it came to pass, when the devil was gone out, the dumb spake; and the people wondered.

djk_text: Ma wantu fu den sama kosi Masaa Jesesi taki: “A nái foondoo wi taki, ai yaki takuu jeje puu a sama tapu. Bika anga Belisebulu, a edeman fu den didibii ai puu den.”
eng_text: But some of them said, He casteth out devils through Beelzebub the chief of the devils.

djk_text: Ma namo, da wanlo sama de ape tesi en luku. Ne den taigi en taki: “Di yu na wan sama fu Masaa Gadu tuutuu, da soi u wan maiki, meke u sabi taki, Masaa Gadu de anga yu anga den sani di yu e du.”
eng_text: And others, tempting him, sought of him a sign from heaven.

djk_text: Ma Masaa Jesesi sabi san de a den baka ede. Ne a taigi den taki: “Efu den sama fu wan kownu kondee opo e feti anga enseefi, da a kondee de, na booko a o booko. Na soseefi, a de anga wan osu pe den sama e libi fanya fanya, feyanti fasi anga denseefi. A osu sama de musu booko saka kaba a soso.
eng_text: But he, knowing their thoughts, said unto them, Every kingdom divided against itself is brought to desolation; and a house divided against a house falleth.

djk_text: Da u taki, mi e wooko anga didibii, fu puu takuu jeje a sama tapu. We, da na feti didibii e feti anga enseefi, fu booko a hii makiti anga a hii kondee fi enseefi, di ai tii.
eng_text: If Satan also be divided against himself, how shall his kingdom stand? because ye say that I cast out devils through Beelzebub.

djk_text: We, di u taki, anga a basi fu didibii mi e puu den takuu jeje, we den sama fu u, no? Anga san den e puu den? Bika denseefi e puu takuu jeje a sama tapu. U go akisi den luku. Da u sa si taki, den sama fu useefi o soi u taki, u ná abi leti.
eng_text: And if I by Beelzebub cast out devils, by whom do your sons cast them out? therefore shall they be your judges.

djk_text: Bika anga a taanga fu Masaa Gadu mi e puu den takuu jeje a sama tapu. Den sani di mi e du anga a taanga fu Masaa Gadu ya, de enke wan maiki fu soi u taki, a Nyun Tii fu Masaa Gadu doo a u mindii now.”
eng_text: But if I with the finger of God cast out devils, no doubt the kingdom of God is come upon you.

djk_text: Ne a taki go doo taki: “Te wan taanga man abi bunbun feti sani fu oli waki ne en osu, da a ná abi fu feele ná wan sani. Bika ná wan sama o poi kon fufuu sani a ini en osu.
eng_text: When a strong man armed keepeth his palace, his goods are in peace:

djk_text: Ma, te wan moo taanga man di abi moo bun feti sani kon feti anga en, da a o fonmi en teke ala den feti sani fi en, puu ne en ana. Da a teke den gudu fi en go paati gi taa sama.”
eng_text: But when a stronger than he shall come upon him, and overcome him, he taketh from him all his armour wherein he trusted, and divideth his spoils.

djk_text: Ne Masaa Jesesi taigi den go doo taki: “A sama di á de anga mi a wanse, da a sama de e feti fu booko mi saka. Da sama di nái wooko makandii anga mi, fu tyai sama kon a mi, sowan sama e yaki den sama paati, puu a mi.”
eng_text: He that is not with me is against me: and he that gathereth not with me scattereth.

djk_text: Ne a taigi den taki: “Te wan takuu jeje komoto a wan sama tapu, da ai waka e lontu e suku peesi na ala den sabana ini, fu boo. Ma a nái poi fende peesi fu boo. Da, te a á poi fende a peesi fu boo, da ai pakisei taki: ‘Meke mi daai go tan na a peesi pe mi be komoto baka.’
eng_text: When the unclean spirit is gone out of a man, he walketh through dry places, seeking rest; and finding none, he saith, I will return unto my house whence I came out.

djk_text: Da te a daai kon baka, a osu pe a be komoto de leigi leigi. A de kiinkiin sibisibi moi silli.
eng_text: And when he cometh, he findeth it swept and garnished.

djk_text: Da ai gwe baka, da a go kai seibin taa takuu jeje, di ogii moo enseefi. Da den e kon na a sama tapu. Da a libi fu sowan sama o moo ogii bakaten, moo enke fa a be de a fesi kaba.”
eng_text: Then goeth he, and taketh to him seven other spirits more wicked than himself; and they enter in, and dwell there: and the last state of that man is worse than the first.

djk_text: Ma, namo di Masaa Jesesi e taki, ne wan uman di be de a ini den sama ini de, bali taki: “Oho! Masaa Gadu seigi a uman di meke yu, fu di Masaa Gadu fende taki, na a uman ya be mu meke yu.”
eng_text: And it came to pass, as he spake these things, a certain woman of the company lifted up her voice, and said unto him, Blessed is the womb that bare thee, and the paps which thou hast sucked.

djk_text: Ne Masaa Jesesi piki en taki: “Uman! I si fa u de ya? Den sama di e aliki Masaa Gadu wowtu e du san a taki, fende moo gaan seigi, moo enke a uman di meke mi.”
eng_text: But he said, Yea rather, blessed are they that hear the word of God, and keep it.

djk_text: Namo somen somen sama e kon a Masaa Jesesi, ne a taki: “Saide meke den sama fu a ten ya abi takuu ati so du? Den e feti fu si maiki fu Gadu. Ma den ná o si ná wan taa maiki moo enke a maiki fu a apaiti takiman fu Masaa Gadu, di den be e kai Jowna.
eng_text: And when the people were gathered thick together, he began to say, This is an evil generation: they seek a sign; and there shall no sign be given it, but the sign of Jonas the prophet.

djk_text: Bika leti enke fa Jowna be de enke wan maiki gi den sama fu Ninifei, na letiso a Manpikin di saka kon toon libisama ya, de enke wan maiki gi den sama fu a ten ya tu.
eng_text: For as Jonas was a sign unto the Ninevites, so shall also the Son of man be to this generation.

djk_text: “A uman kownu fu a kondee di den e kai Seba, na a se fu san dongo, o opo na a gaan kuutu dei, di Masaa Gadu o kuutu sama, fu kuutu den sama fu a ten ya. Bika en dati be komoto langa langa te na a taase fu goontapu fu kon a Salomo, fu kon yee den koni fi en. Ma wan Sama de a u mindii ya, di hei moo Salomo seefi, ma toku, u nái teke en taki.
eng_text: The queen of the south shall rise up in the judgment with the men of this generation, and condemn them: for she came from the utmost parts of the earth to hear the wisdom of Solomon; and, behold, a greater than Solomon is here.

djk_text: Soseefi ala den sama fu Ninifei o opo, da den o kuutu den sama fu a ten ya. Bika den sama fu Ninifei be yee a wowtu fu Masaa Gadu di Jowna be gi den. Ne den teke en, ne den daai libi wanten. Ma wan Sama de a u mindii ya, di hei moo Jowna, ma toku, u nái teke en taki.”
eng_text: The men of Nineve shall rise up in the judgment with this generation, and shall condemn it: for they repented at the preaching of Jonas; and, behold, a greater than Jonas is here.

djk_text: Ne a taigi den taki: “Ná wan sama e leti wan lampu, da a poti en a sani ondoo, efu a teke sani tapu en. Nono! A o poti en a wan hei peesi, fu ala sama di o kon a ini a osu sa si sani bun anga en.
eng_text: No man, when he hath lighted a candle, putteth it in a secret place, neither under a bushel, but on a candlestick, that they which come in may see the light.

djk_text: Da na so a de anga wi libisama tu. U ain, na a lampu fu u sikin. Efu u ain de bunbun, ne u opo den fu si sani, da u o si kiinkiin anga den, fu u sabi san u e du. Ma efu u ain dunguu, da u hii sikin seefi dunguu tu. Bika, wansi u leti wan lampu poti de seefi, toku u ná o si san u e du. Da na ini dunguu u e tan. Da u ná o sabi san u e du.
eng_text: The light of the body is the eye: therefore when thine eye is single, thy whole body also is full of light; but when thine eye is evil, thy body also is full of darkness.

djk_text: A dati meke, u mu e koni fu u á poti u ain fu luku ogii fu u ain anga u ati dunguu.
eng_text: Take heed therefore that the light which is in thee be not darkness.

djk_text: Bika efu u hii ati kiin, sondee fu a abi wan baaka, da u sa leti kiin peesi gi taa sama, leti enke wan lampu di e leti kiin peesi gi sama.”
eng_text: If thy whole body therefore be full of light, having no part dark, the whole shall be full of light, as when the bright shining of a candle doth give thee light.

djk_text: Da Masaa Jesesi kaba taki seefi, ne wan Faliseiman kai en taki: “Masaa Jesesi, kon go nyan anga mi a mi osu, no?” Ne Masaa Jesesi go anga a Faliseiman ne en osu go nyan.
eng_text: And as he spake, a certain Pharisee besought him to dine with him: and he went in, and sat down to meat.

djk_text: Da di den sidon fu nyan, ne wan sani dangaa a Faliseiman. Bika a si taki Masaa Jesesi e nyan, sondee fu wasi ana na a apaiti fasi fa a Dyuweiti be e soi den, fu wasi den ana fosi den go nyan.
eng_text: And when the Pharisee saw it, he marvelled that he had not first washed before dinner.

djk_text: Da di Masaa Jesesi si taki a sani ya dangaa a Faliseiman, ne a taigi en taki: “U Faliseiman! U e wasi u sikin namo, da u kaba, fu soi kiin a doose. Ma u ati lai anga giili anga takuudu!
eng_text: And the Lord said unto him, Now do ye Pharisees make clean the outside of the cup and the platter; but your inward part is full of ravening and wickedness.

djk_text: U wisiwasi sani sondee fusutan! U e feti namo fu wasi doose fu u sikin kiin. Ma fa fu u ati? U á sabi taki, Masaa Gadu wani meke u wasi u ati kiin tu, no?
eng_text: Ye fools, did not he that made that which is without make that which is within also?

djk_text: U feti fu wasi u ati kiin, fu u yeepi den pooti sama a sani. Da te u ati kiin so kaba, da u ná abi fu feti, fu wasi ana moo enke fa u gwenti. Bika efu u ati kiin, da ala sani fu u kiin tu.”
eng_text: But rather give alms of such things as ye have; and, behold, all things are clean unto you.

djk_text: Ne Masaa Jesesi taki go doo taki: “Heelu fu u enke Faliseiman de! Bika u nái libi letiopu anga sama, anga u á lobi Masaa Gadu tu. Ma u e paati ala san u abi a tin pisi, da u e gi Masaa Gadu wan fu den tin pisi. Soseefi u e gi en wan pisi fu tin, fu ala u goon nyanyan enke fa a Dyuweiti taki. Da u e si enke u bun kaba. We, a ná enke fu gi Masaa Gadu wan pisi fu tin, fu ala san u abi, ná ogii. Ma dati á sai. Bika feti fu libi letiopu anga ala lobi Masaa Gadu seefi tu.”
eng_text: But woe unto you, Pharisees! for ye tithe mint and rue and all manner of herbs, and pass over judgment and the love of God: these ought ye to have done, and not to leave the other undone.

djk_text: Ne a taki moo taki: “Heelu ete wan toon, fu u enke Faliseiman! Bika te u go a keliki, da u lobi sidon a den fesiman sutuu a ini a keliki. Soseefi, te u e waka a ganda, da u e wani meke ala sama e gi u odi a sama fesi, enke u hei moo ala taa sama.
eng_text: Woe unto you, Pharisees! for ye love the uppermost seats in the synagogues, and greetings in the markets.

djk_text: We, heelu fu u! Bika u de leti enke gaandi geebi, di sama e waka e pasa a den tapu, sondee fu den sabi taki, a sowan ogii tapu, den e waka e pasa de.”
eng_text: Woe unto you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! for ye are as graves which appear not, and the men that walk over them are not aware of them.

djk_text: Ne wan leliman fu Dyuweiti bali gi en taki: “We, Mesiti, oo! Fa yu e kosi den Faliseiman de, u de a ini tu?”
eng_text: Then answered one of the lawyers, and said unto him, Master, thus saying thou reproachest us also.

djk_text: Ne Masaa Jesesi kosi den now taki: “Heelu fu u enke leliman fu weiti! Bika u e leli den sama Masaa Gadu weiti, da u e suku fu poti ibi a den sama neki tapu, fu den tyai. Ma useefi nái meke moiti, fu diki wan pikinso fu dati tyai seefi.
eng_text: And he said, Woe unto you also, ye lawyers! for ye lade men with burdens grievous to be borne, and ye yourselves touch not the burdens with one of your fingers.

djk_text: Da heelu fu u! Bika u e seeka den geebi fu den apaiti fositen apaiti takiman fu Masaa Gadu. We, na den avo gaansama fu u be kii den.
eng_text: Woe unto you! for ye build the sepulchres of the prophets, and your fathers killed them.

djk_text: Da anga dati, u e soi taki, a bun gi u fa den gaansama fu u kii den fositen apaiti takiman fu Masaa Gadu. Da efu u be de a den peesi, na a seefi sani u be sa du tu. Den gaansama kii. Den pikin e seeka geebi.
eng_text: Truly ye bear witness that ye allow the deeds of your fathers: for they indeed killed them, and ye build their sepulchres.

djk_text: Ma a ná ogii. Masaa Gadu sabi fa a o du anga u. Bika Masaa Gadu be taki a fesi kaba taki, a sende a apaiti takiman anga apaiti bosikopuman kon gi u. Ma u o kii son fu den. Da taawan u o yaki gwe.
eng_text: Therefore also said the wisdom of God, I will send them prophets and apostles, and some of them they shall slay and persecute:

djk_text: “Na fu dati ede meke, Masaa Gadu o akisi u faantiwowtu, fu ala den apaiti takiman fi en di u be kii fanafu goontapu sete.
eng_text: That the blood of all the prophets, which was shed from the foundation of the world, may be required of this generation;

djk_text: Fu a Abeli, a fosi sama di u kii, te go miti Sakalia, di u be kii a Mama Keliki, koosube fu a apaiti begi tafaa. U o tyai a sitaafu fu ala den fiya.”
eng_text: From the blood of Abel unto the blood of Zacharias, which perished between the altar and the temple: verily I say unto you, It shall be required of this generation.

djk_text: Ne Masaa Jesesi taki go doo taki: “We, heelu fu u enke leliman fu weiti! San meke u abi takuudu so du? Bika u e kibii a tuutuu leli gi den sama, fu den á sa poi sabi en. Ma u seefi nái meke moiti fu du san den weiti taki. Da u e tapu pasi gi den sama di wani kon sabi den.”
eng_text: Woe unto you, lawyers! for ye have taken away the key of knowledge: ye entered not in yourselves, and them that were entering in ye hindered.

djk_text: Da, di Masaa Jesesi taki den sani ya, ne den Faliseiman anga den leliman fu weiti ati teke faya.
eng_text: And as he said these things unto them, the scribes and the Pharisees began to urge him vehemently, and to provoke him to speak of many things:

djk_text: Ne fanafu a dei de, ne den e akisi en somen sani, fu tesi en, fu a taki sani di á bun, fu den tyai en go kaagi.
eng_text: Laying wait for him, and seeking to catch something out of his mouth, that they might accuse him.

djk_text: Da a yuu di Masaa Jesesi e taki de, ne onmen dunsu sama e kon ne en, te den e banda denseefi. Ma namo, ne Masaa Jesesi daai, ne a bali den bakaman fi en taki: “U mu luku bun anga a sowda fu den Faliseiman. Den e meke enke den na bunbun sama, ma na soso ogii. Mi bali u. U á libi enke den!
eng_text: In the mean time, when there were gathered together an innumerable multitude of people, insomuch that they trode one upon another, he began to say unto his disciples first of all, Beware ye of the leaven of the Pharisees, which is hypocrisy.

djk_text: Bika ná wan sani sa de a kibii te, da a á kon a doo. Soseefi ná wan sani sa pasa bakabaka te, da a á kon fu sama sabi.
eng_text: For there is nothing covered, that shall not be revealed; neither hid, that shall not be known.

djk_text: Da ala san u taki a dunguu, den o yee a gaan dei. Da ala san u taigi useefi a yesi a ini kambaa, den o taampu a osu tapu bali den gi kondee.”
eng_text: Therefore whatsoever ye have spoken in darkness shall be heard in the light; and that which ye have spoken in the ear in closets shall be proclaimed upon the housetops.

djk_text: Ne Masaa Jesesi taigi den bakaman taki: “Mi mati! Mi e taigi yu tuutuu taki, yu á mu feele den sama di sa kii yu sikin namo, da bakadati den á poi du ná wan sani anga yu moo.
eng_text: And I say unto you my friends, Be not afraid of them that kill the body, and after that have no more that they can do.

djk_text: Ma mi o soi yu sama yu mu feele. Na Awan di abi a taanga fu kii yu, te a kaba, da a towe yu go a ini didibii faya . Tuutuu! Ne en i mu feele!
eng_text: But I will forewarn you whom ye shall fear: Fear him, which after he hath killed hath power to cast into hell; yea, I say unto you, Fear him.

djk_text: “Bika u luku ala den pikin foo di e fee a tapu. Den e seli feifi fu den fu tu tiisensi. Bika sama e si den enke soso sani, ma toku Masaa Gadu nái feegete ná wan fu den. We, efu Masaa Gadu nái feegete ná wan fu den pikin foo di e fee a tapu anda, da fa fu u enke libisama, di hei moo enke den pikin foo? We, Masaa Gadu sabi u, te doo onmen sii uwii de a u ede seefi, a sabi.”
eng_text: Are not five sparrows sold for two farthings, and not one of them is forgotten before God?

djk_text: We ne, di a taki so kaba, ne a taigi den taki: “Sama di sa piki a fesi fu libisama taki, a sabi a Manpikin di saka kon toon libisama ya, da enseefi sa piki baka taki, enseefi sabi en tu, a fesi fu den Basiya fu Masaa Gadu Kondee, a tapu.
eng_text: Also I say unto you, Whosoever shall confess me before men, him shall the Son of man also confess before the angels of God:

djk_text: Ma sama di á wani piki a fesi fu libisama taki, a sabi mi, da miseefi ná o piki, a fesi fu den Basiya fu Masaa Gadu Kondee a tapu taki, mi sabi en tu.”
eng_text: But he that denieth me before men shall be denied before the angels of God.

djk_text: Ne a taki go doo taki: “Ma fu tuu, efu wan sama kosi a Manpikin di saka kon toon libisama ya, da Masaa Gadu sa gi en paadon. Ma efu wan sama e kosi a Apaiti Jeje fu Masaa Gadu, da noiti a o gi en paadon fu dati.”
eng_text: And whosoever shall speak a word against the Son of man, it shall be forgiven him: but unto him that blasphemeth against the Holy Ghost it shall not be forgiven.

djk_text: Ne Masaa Jesesi taigi den baka taki: “Te den kisi u tyai go a kuutu a den keliki osu fu den, efu te den kisi u tyai go a den gaansama anga den gaaman fu kondee fu kuutu u, da u ati á mu piiti fu pakisei taki: ‘San u o taki?’
eng_text: And when they bring you unto the synagogues, and unto magistrates, and powers, take ye no thought how or what thing ye shall answer, or what ye shall say:

djk_text: Bika, te a yuu doo, da a Apaiti Jeje fu Masaa Gadu seefi o gi u san, fu taki.”
eng_text: For the Holy Ghost shall teach you in the same hour what ye ought to say.

djk_text: Ne a seefi yuu de, ne wan sama bali a mindii fu den somen sama de taki: “Mesiti! Mi begi i baa, gaantangi. Taigi mi baala, meke a gi mi fu mi se gudu di wi dda dede fika gi u.”
eng_text: And one of the company said unto him, Master, speak to my brother, that he divide the inheritance with me.

djk_text: Ne Masaa Jesesi piki en taki: “Sama poti mi fu koti kuutu paati u gudu gi u?”
eng_text: And he said unto him, Man, who made me a judge or a divider over you?

djk_text: Ne a taigi den sama di taampu de taki: “U mu koni bun anga useefi, fu u ná abi giili ati. U á feti fu fende sani di u ná abi fanowdu. Bika a ná gudu e meke wan sama libi langa ofu libi switi.”
eng_text: And he said unto them, Take heed, and beware of covetousness: for a man's life consisteth not in the abundance of the things which he possesseth.

djk_text: Ne Masaa Jesesi gi den wan toli taki: “Wan guduman be koti wan goon fi en. Ne a paandi en, te a kaba. Da a goon meke nyanyan fu tyobo.”
eng_text: And he spake a parable unto them, saying, The ground of a certain rich man brought forth plentifully:

djk_text: Ne a man sidon, ne a pakisei taki: “San mi o du? Bika mi ná abi magisin sai fu poti a nyanyan ya.”
eng_text: And he thought within himself, saying, What shall I do, because I have no room where to bestow my fruits?

djk_text: Ne a de te wan pisi, ne a taki: “Mi sabi kaba san mi o du. Mi o booko den pikin osu fu mi puu, da mi meke moo gaanwan fu poti a nyanyan anga a gudu fu mi.
eng_text: And he said, This will I do: I will pull down my barns, and build greater; and there will I bestow all my fruits and my goods.

djk_text: Da now, mi de enke fa mi wani. Mi abi nyanyan fu onmen yali. A á de fu mi wooko moo. Mi sa nyan diingi meke piisii enke fa mi wani.”
eng_text: And I will say to my soul, Soul, thou hast much goods laid up for many years; take thine ease, eat, drink, and be merry.

djk_text: Ma te fu a poti pakisei, ne Masaa Gadu taigi en taki: “I lawman yu! Sama taigi i a sani de! A seefi neti ya, a libi boo fi yu sa komoto a yu gwe. Da sama yu o fika den gudu fi yu anga a somen nyanyan fi i di i seeka poti de gi?”
eng_text: But God said unto him, Thou fool, this night thy soul shall be required of thee: then whose shall those things be, which thou hast provided?

djk_text: Ne Masaa Jesesi taigi den taki: “U si! Na so e pasa anga den sama fu a goontapu ya, di e suku fu fende gudu naamo, sondee fu feti fu libi enke fa Masaa Gadu wani, fu den fende gudu ne en anda.”
eng_text: So is he that layeth up treasure for himself, and is not rich toward God.

djk_text: Ne Masaa Jesesi daai, ne a taki anga den bakaman fi en baka taki: “U á mu booko u ede taki, san u o nyan ofu san u o wei.
eng_text: And he said unto his disciples, Therefore I say unto you, Take no thought for your life, what ye shall eat; neither for the body, what ye shall put on.

djk_text: Bika Masaa Gadu gi wi sikin anga libi di de moo enke koosi anga nyanyan. Da efu a sikin anga a libi di Masaa Gadu gi u de moo enke koosi anga nyanyan, da u denki taki, a ná o gi u koosi fu wei anga nyanyan fu nyan?
eng_text: The life is more than meat, and the body is more than raiment.

djk_text: We, luku den foo a tapu! Den nái koti goon paandi nyanyan. Soseefi, den ná abi kedee efu baakoto e kibii nyanyan fu nyan taa dei baka. Ma toku, den e nyan e diingi ibii dei. Bika Masaa Gadu e solugu den. We, u libisama, no? U á waiti moo den foo, no? Da Masaa Gadu sa fika u sondee koosi efu sondee nyanyan?
eng_text: Consider the ravens: for they neither sow nor reap; which neither have storehouse nor barn; and God feedeth them: how much more are ye better than the fowls?

djk_text: Sama de di sa booko en ede te, da a libi moo langa moo enke san Masaa Gadu poti gi en?
eng_text: And which of you with taking thought can add to his stature one cubit?

djk_text: We, efu booko ede á poi yeepi yu a den pikin sani de, da fu saide meke yu e booko yu ede anga den gaan sani?
eng_text: If ye then be not able to do that thing which is least, why take ye thought for the rest?

djk_text: “We, luku den boomiki a ini sabana, fa den moi. Den nái wooko. Soseefi den nái nai sani fu wei tu. Ma mi e taigi u taki, anga ala fa Salomo, a fositen kownu fu Islayeli Kondee be e wei moi, toku a á be wei moi kisi den boomiki ya.
eng_text: Consider the lilies how they grow: they toil not, they spin not; and yet I say unto you, that Solomon in all his glory was not arrayed like one of these.

djk_text: Efu Masaa Gadu wei den boomiki so moi, da san na yu di hei moo ala den boomiki ya? Bika tide yu e si den, ma tamaa den á de moo. Kee! Libisama, saide meke a biibi di u abi a Masaa Gadu swaki so du?
eng_text: If then God so clothe the grass, which is to day in the field, and to morrow is cast into the oven; how much more will he clothe you, O ye of little faith?

djk_text: U á booko u ede anga san u o nyan ofu san u o diingi. U á mu si nyanyan anga diingi enke gaan sani.
eng_text: And seek not ye what ye shall eat, or what ye shall drink, neither be ye of doubtful mind.

djk_text: Bika na sama di á sabi Masaa Gadu e booko den ede anga den sowtu sani de. Ma u Tata di de a tapu sabi san u abi fanowdu.
eng_text: For all these things do the nations of the world seek after: and your Father knoweth that ye have need of these things.

djk_text: Ma suku fu de a ini a Nyun Tii fu Masaa Gadu. Da a o gi u ala san u fanowdu.”
eng_text: But rather seek ye the kingdom of God; and all these things shall be added unto you.

djk_text: Namo a taigi den bakaman fi en go doo taki: “Mi mati! U nái ipi, ma u á mu feele. Bika a be bun gi Masaa Gadu, u Tata, fu a be teke u poti a ini a Nyun Tii fi en, fu u be sa fende a bun fi en.
eng_text: Fear not, little flock; for it is your Father's good pleasure to give you the kingdom.

djk_text: U á mu feti fu suku gudu dyunta, poti a goontapu ya namo. Ma u seli den, da u paati a moni gi den pootiman. Na sowan fasi u sa kibii gudu a Masaa Gadu, di ná o poi kaba noiti moo, a Masaa Gadu Kondee anda. Fufuuman ná o poi go anda go fufuu den. Soseefi woon ná o nyanmi den tu. Da na Masaa Gadu i mu kibii i gudu poti. Da noiti den sa poli.
eng_text: Sell that ye have, and give alms; provide yourselves bags which wax not old, a treasure in the heavens that faileth not, where no thief approacheth, neither moth corrupteth.

djk_text: Bika na pe i gudu de, na ape i ati o de tu!”
eng_text: For where your treasure is, there will your heart be also.

djk_text: Ne a taigi den bakaman fi en baka taki: “U seeka useefi, de kaba kaba e luku u Masaa. U meke a faya fu u de leti leti.
eng_text: Let your loins be girded about, and your lights burning;

djk_text: “U mu de leti enke den futuboi di den masaa go a wan gaan fesa. Ne den de kaba kaba e luku on ten a masaa fu den o kon. Da te a masaa kon, da den sa opo doo gi en wanten. Bika den de kaba kaba.
eng_text: And ye yourselves like unto men that wait for their lord, when he will return from the wedding; that when he cometh and knocketh, they may open unto him immediately.

djk_text: Seigi fu a futuboi di de kaba kaba e luku en masaa. Bika a masaa seefi o seeka tafaa, te a kaba, da a kai en fu kon sidon nyan anga en. Enseefi o koti nyanyan paati gi den dati.
eng_text: Blessed are those servants, whom the lord when he cometh shall find watching: verily I say unto you, that he shall gird himself, and make them to sit down to meat, and will come forth and serve them.

djk_text: Da a o de wan seigi gi ala futuboi di de kaba kaba e luku den masaa. “Da meke u de kaba kaba e luku u Masaa tu. Efu na neti ofu na musude a o kon, a ná abi toobi. U mu de kaba kaba!
eng_text: And if he shall come in the second watch, or come in the third watch, and find them so, blessed are those servants.

djk_text: “Ma u oli disi bun a ede. Wan sama di sabi taki, na so wan yuu fufuuman o kon fufuu ne en osu, o de anga ain e luku a fufuuman. A ná o meke a fufuuman booko en osu, fu fufuu en sani.
eng_text: And this know, that if the goodman of the house had known what hour the thief would come, he would have watched, and not have suffered his house to be broken through.

djk_text: A moo bun, efu u de kaba kaba alaten. Bika, a Manpikin di saka kon toon libisama ya o daai kon baka, a wan yuu di libisama á poti pakisei.”
eng_text: Be ye therefore ready also: for the Son of man cometh at an hour when ye think not.

djk_text: Da di Masaa Jesesi taki so, te a kaba, ne Peitilisi akisi en taki: “Masaa! Den sani di yu e taigi u ya, na fu ala sama, ofu na fu u wawan?”
eng_text: Then Peter said unto him, Lord, speakest thou this parable unto us, or even to all?

djk_text: Ne Masaa Jesesi piki en taki: “Mi e taki fu wan futuboi di en masaa be sende, fu gi ibii taa sama a ini a osu, en pisi fu a nyanyan, na a leti yuu.
eng_text: And the Lord said, Who then is that faithful and wise steward, whom his lord shall make ruler over his household, to give them their portion of meat in due season?

djk_text: We, te a masaa o kon doo baka, da seigi fu a futuboi de. A masaa o pai en gaan paiman, efu a si taki: ‘Aai! A futuboi ya e wooko enke fa a fiti gi mi.’
eng_text: Blessed is that servant, whom his lord when he cometh shall find so doing.

djk_text: Da fu tuu, mi e taigi u, a masaa de o poti a futuboi toon a basi, di e luku ala en gudu. Na so a masaa ya o du.
eng_text: Of a truth I say unto you, that he will make him ruler over all that he hath.

djk_text: Ma meke u taki, a futuboi be pakisei taki: ‘Mi basi ná o kon ete.’ Da a bigin go nyan, diingi anga duunguman. Soseefi ai fon den taawan, uman anga man a ini a osu fu a masaa.
eng_text: But and if that servant say in his heart, My lord delayeth his coming; and shall begin to beat the menservants and maidens, and to eat and drink, and to be drunken;

djk_text: We, da a masaa be o kon a wan dei, anga wan yuu di a futuboi ya á poti pakisei. Bika a futuboi seefi á sabi on dei a masaa o kon baka. Da a masaa be o meke den doo a futuboi ede. Da a poti en go a pe fu sitaafu den sama di nái teke Masaa Gadu taki.
eng_text: The lord of that servant will come in a day when he looketh not for him, and at an hour when he is not aware, and will cut him in sunder, and will appoint him his portion with the unbelievers.

djk_text: Bika, efu wan futuboi sabi san en masaa wani a mu du, ma a nái seeka fu du dati, da a sa fende wan tumisi gaan fonfon.
eng_text: And that servant, which knew his lord's will, and prepared not himself, neither did according to his will, shall be beaten with many stripes.

djk_text: “Da a sama di e du wan sani sondee sabi, o kisi lekiti sitaafu. Ma a sama di e du sani anga sabi, da a o kisi ibi sitaafu. Efu wan sama kisi ipi wooko, fu de enke basi fu den, da den o akisi en ipi faantiwowtu tu. On moo ipi wan sama kisi, on moo bigi a faantiwowtu fi en de tu.”
eng_text: But he that knew not, and did commit things worthy of stripes, shall be beaten with few stripes. For unto whomsoever much is given, of him shall be much required: and to whom men have committed much, of him they will ask the more.

djk_text: Ne Masaa Jesesi taigi den taki: “A kon mi kon a goontapu, fu sutu faya gi goontapu enke fa den sama e sutu faya boon wan goon. Da a be sa moo bun gi mi, efu a faya ya be sutu kaba.
eng_text: I am come to send fire on the earth; and what will I if it be already kindled?

djk_text: A sitaafu di mi mu tyai fosi mi sutu a faya ya, na wan hebi sitaafu. Da a ibi gi mi tuu.
eng_text: But I have a baptism to be baptized with; and how am I straitened till it be accomplished!

djk_text: Da san u be denki? U be denki taki, na fii fasi fu libisama libi anga denseefi, tyai kon a goontapu? Nono! Ná dati mi tyai kon. Mi kon fu paati sama anga sama.
eng_text: Suppose ye that I am come to give peace on earth? I tell you, Nay; but rather division:

djk_text: Fanafu now, da efu feifi sama de a ini wan osu, da den o meke toobi anga denseefi fu mi ede. Dii o de a wanse anga mi, da tu de a wan taase. Ofu tu o de a mi se, da dii de na a taase.
eng_text: For from henceforth there shall be five in one house divided, three against two, and two against three.

djk_text: Wan dda anga en manpikin o poli fu mi ede. Da wan mma anga en umanpikin o poli fu mi ede. Soseefi wan mma anga a uman fi en manpikin o poli.”
eng_text: The father shall be divided against the son, and the son against the father; the mother against the daughter, and the daughter against the mother; the mother in law against her daughter in law, and the daughter in law against her mother in law.

djk_text: Ne di Masaa Jesesi daai, ne a taki anga den somen sama di kon ne en de now taki: “Te u luku tapu, ne u si wan woluku na a se fu san opo, da u e taki alen o kon. Da ai kon tuu.
eng_text: And he said also to the people, When ye see a cloud rise out of the west, straightway ye say, There cometh a shower; and so it is.

djk_text: Te a winta e wai komoto a opuse, da u e taki: ‘A san o ati.’ Da ai ati tuu.
eng_text: And when ye see the south wind blow, ye say, There will be heat; and it cometh to pass.

djk_text: U soso mofu libisama! Te u luku tapu, u e si efu alen o kai, efu san o pii. Dati u sabi bun. Ma saide meke u á wani opo u ain, fu si den maiki di e pasa leti a u fesi a goontapu a doti ya? Na si u nái si den sani ya, fu sabi on yuu ten fu goontapu u de?
eng_text: Ye hypocrites, ye can discern the face of the sky and of the earth; but how is it that ye do not discern this time?

djk_text: “Bika u sabi, san di bun fu du anga san di á bun fu du. Da saide meke u nái luku san di de leti fu du?
eng_text: Yea, and why even of yourselves judge ye not what is right?

djk_text: Bika efu yu anga yu feyanti abi toobi, ne i si taki a wani tyai yu go a kuutu, da i mu meke moiti fu taki fiti anga en, fosi u doo a kuutuman. Ma efu yu á du dati, da den o iti yu go a ini dunguu osu.
eng_text: When thou goest with thine adversary to the magistrate, as thou art in the way, give diligence that thou mayest be delivered from him; lest he hale thee to the judge, and the judge deliver thee to the officer, and the officer cast thee into prison.

djk_text: Da yu ná o komoto, de fu te enke i pai a lasiti kopoo sensi di den naki lenti gi yu, fu pai.”
eng_text: I tell thee, thou shalt not depart thence, till thou hast paid the very last mite.

djk_text: Ne a seefi yuu de, ne wanlo sama kon taigi Masaa Jesesi taki, den suudati fu Gaaman Pilatesi kii wan duupu Galileya sama, di be de a ini a Mama Keliki e kii wan meti, fu boon enke paiman, fu begi Masaa Gadu. Ne den towe den mokisa den buulu anga a meti di den be e kii de.
eng_text: There were present at that season some that told him of the Galilaeans, whose blood Pilate had mingled with their sacrifices.

djk_text: Ne Masaa Jesesi akisi den taki: “U membee taki, na fu di den sama de be e libi takuu moo ala den taa sama fu Galileya, meke den suudati kii den?
eng_text: And Jesus answering said unto them, Suppose ye that these Galilaeans were sinners above all the Galilaeans, because they suffered such things?

djk_text: Nono! Ná dati meke a ogii de pasa anga den. Bika efu useefi á daai libi, da na letiso a sa pasa anga u tu.”
eng_text: I tell you, Nay: but, except ye repent, ye shall all likewise perish.

djk_text: Ne a akisi den baka taki: “San u pakisei fu den tin na aitin sama di a tolen fu Silowam be booko kai kii? U membee taki na fu di den sama de be e libi takuu moo ala taa sama fu Jelusalem meke den sani de pasa anga den?
eng_text: Or those eighteen, upon whom the tower in Siloam fell, and slew them, think ye that they were sinners above all men that dwelt in Jerusalem?

djk_text: Nono! A ná fu di den ogii moo u. Mi e taigi u tuutuu. Efu u á daai libi, da na letiso useefi sa dede kaba a soso tu.”
eng_text: I tell you, Nay: but, except ye repent, ye shall all likewise perish.

djk_text: Ne a gi den wan toli taki: “Wan yali ten, da wan sama be paandi wan sii den e kai figasii a ini en goon. Ne, di a sama de, te wan dei, ne a go na a goon fi en go suku nyanyan na a figasii bon. Ma a á fende ná wan kodo nyanyan ne en.
eng_text: He spake also this parable; A certain man had a fig tree planted in his vineyard; and he came and sought fruit thereon, and found none.

djk_text: Ne a taigi a man di a be poti e luku a goon taki: ‘Faa a bon ya towe. Bika na fu soso a taampu a ini a goon ya! Na dii yali langa kaba di mi e kon e suku nyanyan na a bon ya, sondee fu fende wan kodo.’
eng_text: Then said he unto the dresser of his vineyard, Behold, these three years I come seeking fruit on this fig tree, and find none: cut it down; why cumbereth it the ground?

djk_text: “Ne a man di e luku a goon taki: ‘Basi! Meke u fika en wan yali ete, baa? Mi o puu gotoo lontu en, da mi o poti doti gi en.
eng_text: And he answering said unto him, Lord, let it alone this year also, till I shall dig about it, and dung it:

djk_text: Da kande a sa gi nyanyan. Ma efu a á meke ná wan nyanyan, da te i daai kon baka, da i sa faa en towe tuu.’ ”
eng_text: And if it bear fruit, well: and if not, then after that thou shalt cut it down.

djk_text: Ne wan dei, ne Masaa Jesesi go a ini wan Dyu keliki go e leli den sama Masaa Gadu wowtu.
eng_text: And he was teaching in one of the synagogues on the sabbath.

djk_text: Da di a leli, te wan pisi, ne en ain kai anga wan uman a ini a keliki osu. A uman ya be siki te, a fika bukubuku. A á poi opo en ede luku tapu moo seefi. Na tin na aitin yali kaba, di a de anga a siki ya. Da na wan takuu sani namo, i si be siki en poti so.
eng_text: And, behold, there was a woman which had a spirit of infirmity eighteen years, and was bowed together, and could in no wise lift up herself.

djk_text: Ne Masaa Jesesi kai a uman kon ne en! Ne a taigi en taki: “Uman! I kon bun fu a siki ya!”
eng_text: And when Jesus saw her, he called her to him, and said unto her, Woman, thou art loosed from thine infirmity.

djk_text: Ne a poti ana na a uman ya tapu, ne wanten a uman opo taampu tiloo enke fa a be de fosi. Ne a gafa Masaa Gadu gi en daa.
eng_text: And he laid his hands on her: and immediately she was made straight, and glorified God.

djk_text: Ma a á bun gi a edeman fu a Dyu keliki, fa Masaa Jesesi deesi a uman na a kina dei ya. Ne a akisi den sama taki: “A ná sigisi dei a wiki abi, fu wooko, no? Da saide meke u nái kon a wan fu den sigisi dei ya, fu suku yeepi fu u siki? U á kon a kina dei kon suku yeepi fu u siki, moo.”
eng_text: And the ruler of the synagogue answered with indignation, because that Jesus had healed on the sabbath day, and said unto the people, There are six days in which men ought to work: in them therefore come and be healed, and not on the sabbath day.

djk_text: Namo Masaa Jesesi piki en taki: “I bidiigiman yu! Iseefi e wooko a kina dei. Bika ala kina dei, u e losi den kaw anga den buliki fu u tyai go diingi wataa.
eng_text: The Lord then answered him, and said, Thou hypocrite, doth not each one of you on the sabbath loose his ox or his ass from the stall, and lead him away to watering?

djk_text: We, a uman ya, no? Wan bakapikin fu Abalaham, di a didibii tei tin na aitin yali langa a sitaafu. Da na fu di na kina dei ede, meke a tetei di tei en á mu losi?”
eng_text: And ought not this woman, being a daughter of Abraham, whom Satan hath bound, lo, these eighteen years, be loosed from this bond on the sabbath day?

djk_text: We, di Masaa Jesesi taki so, ne sen kisi den di be e sitee anga den, te ná sipowtu. Ma den taa sama piisii te, fu den gaan foondoo sani di Masaa Jesesi e du.
eng_text: And when he had said these things, all his adversaries were ashamed: and all the people rejoiced for all the glorious things that were done by him.

djk_text: Da, ne Masaa Jesesi akisi den baka taki: “Anga san mi sa maiki a Nyun Tii fu Masaa Gadu?
eng_text: Then said he, Unto what is the kingdom of God like? and whereunto shall I resemble it?

djk_text: We, a de enke wan sii den e kai mosite, di wan sama paandi ne en goon. A sii ya na wan pikintoin sii, pikinmoo ain á poi si en. Ma, te den paandi en, te a goo, da ai bigi moo ala den taa sani di den paandi a ini a goon. Den ana fi en e bigi paati, te den foo e meke nesi e teke koo a den. Da na so a Nyun Tii fu Masaa Gadu de.”
eng_text: It is like a grain of mustard seed, which a man took, and cast into his garden; and it grew, and waxed a great tree; and the fowls of the air lodged in the branches of it.

djk_text: Ne a akisi den baka taki: “San moo mi sa teke maiki a Nyun Tii fu Masaa Gadu?
eng_text: And again he said, Whereunto shall I liken the kingdom of God?

djk_text: We, a de enke wan pikintoin sowda di wan uman teke iti a ini wan gaan tyaipi bolon. Da a sowda soopu ala a bolon, te doo. Na so a Nyun Tii fu Masaa Gadu de.”
eng_text: It is like leaven, which a woman took and hid in three measures of meal, till the whole was leavened.

djk_text: Ne bakadati, ne Masaa Jesesi komoto de e go a Jelusalem. Da ai leli den sama fu den kondee kondee pe ai pasa, Masaa Gadu wowtu.
eng_text: And he went through the cities and villages, teaching, and journeying toward Jerusalem.

djk_text: Ne wan sama akisi en taki: “Masaa! Na pikinso sama namo o go a Masaa Gadu?” Ne Masaa Jesesi piki en taki:
eng_text: Then said one unto him, Lord, are there few that be saved? And he said unto them,

djk_text: “Feti fi i seefi sa de wan fu den sama di o doo pasa go a ini a sumaa doo mofu. Bika mi e taigi u taki, somen fu u o feti, fu pasa go a ini a pikin doo ya, ma den ná o poi.
eng_text: Strive to enter in at the strait gate: for many, I say unto you, will seek to enter in, and shall not be able.

djk_text: Da u o de ape, fu te enke a basi fu a osu kon sooto a doo. Da u o de ape na a baka doo e naki e begi taki: ‘Masaa, gaantangi! Opo a doo gi u, baa?’ Ma a basi fu a osu o piki u taki: ‘Mi á sabi u! On se u komoto kon ya?’
eng_text: When once the master of the house is risen up, and hath shut to the door, and ye begin to stand without, and to knock at the door, saying, Lord, Lord, open unto us; and he shall answer and say unto you, I know you not whence ye are:

djk_text: “Da u o piki en taki: ‘Masaa, i sabi u! Na u anga i be e nyan e diingi. I be de a u kondee ganda e leli wi Masaa Gadu wowtu ibii yuu.’
eng_text: Then shall ye begin to say, We have eaten and drunk in thy presence, and thou hast taught in our streets.

djk_text: Da a sa piki u taki: ‘Mi taigi u kaba taki, mi á sabi u. Mi á sabi on se u komoto kon ya. U gwe komoto ya, u takuu ati sani u! Bika u á be wani poti yesi aliki fu du san Masaa Gadu be e taigi u.’
eng_text: But he shall say, I tell you, I know you not whence ye are; depart from me, all ye workers of iniquity.

djk_text: “Da u o de ape e kaw tifi e kee gaan kee. Bika u sa si u avo Abalaham, Isaki, Jakowbesi anga ala den apaiti takiman fu Masaa Gadu, a ini a Nyun Tii fu Masaa Gadu Kondee. Ma useefi á poi go doo a den.
eng_text: There shall be weeping and gnashing of teeth, when ye shall see Abraham, and Isaac, and Jacob, and all the prophets, in the kingdom of God, and you yourselves thrust out.

djk_text: Da somen sama o komoto na ala se fu goontapu go doo a ini a Nyun Tii a Masaa Gadu Kondee. Da ala den o sidon a tafaa anda.
eng_text: And they shall come from the east, and from the west, and from the north, and from the south, and shall sit down in the kingdom of God.

djk_text: Da mi e taigi u taki, a ini Masaa Gadu, somen sama di de fesiwan ya o toon bakaman. Da somen di de bakaman ya o daai toon fesiwan.”
eng_text: And, behold, there are last which shall be first, and there are first which shall be last.

djk_text: Ma namo, da a seefi yuu de, ne wantu Faliseiman kon taigi Masaa Jesesi taki: “Gwe komoto ya esi esi! Bika Kownu Helowdesi e suku i fu kii.”
eng_text: The same day there came certain of the Pharisees, saying unto him, Get thee out, and depart hence: for Herod will kill thee.

djk_text: Ne Masaa Jesesi piki den taki: “U go taigi a lei mofu bidiigiman de taki: ‘Tide anga tamaa, mi o de ya ete e yaki takuu jeje puu a sama tapu. Soseefi mi e go doo, fu deesi den siki sama kon bun baka tu. Ma di fu dii dei, da mi o kaba.
eng_text: And he said unto them, Go ye, and tell that fox, Behold, I cast out devils, and I do cures to day and to morrow, and the third day I shall be perfected.

djk_text: Winsi fa, mi musu fu waka wantu dei ete, fosi mi doo Jelusalem. Bika den nái kii wan apaiti takiman fu Masaa Gadu a wan taa peesi moo enke Jelusalem Foto.’ ”
eng_text: Nevertheless I must walk to day, and to morrow, and the day following: for it cannot be that a prophet perish out of Jerusalem.

djk_text: Ne Masaa Jesesi daai taki sani fu den sama fu Jelusalem taki: “Sama fu Jelusalem! Na den apaiti takiman fu Masaa Gadu u kii so? Oho! Den sama di Masaa Gadu sende kon fu taki sani fu Masaa Gadu, ne u naki anga siton e kii? Ma a tyali! Bika u sabi onmen toon mi kai u, fu u kon a mi, fu mi kibii u, leti enke fa wan uman foo e kai den pikin fi en kon kibii ne en mapaapi ondoo? Ma kweti! U á wani dati. Da a tyali!
eng_text: O Jerusalem, Jerusalem, which killest the prophets, and stonest them that are sent unto thee; how often would I have gathered thy children together, as a hen doth gather her brood under her wings, and ye would not!

djk_text: Na dati meke Masaa Gadu fika a kondee gi u, fu u du enke fa u sabi. Ma mi dati, u ná o si mi moo. Mi o gwe. Ma wan ten e kon, da u o si mi baka. Da u sa bali baaya taki: ‘Seigi fu Awan di e kon a ini a nen fu Masaa!’ ”
eng_text: Behold, your house is left unto you desolate: and verily I say unto you, Ye shall not see me, until the time come when ye shall say, Blessed is he that cometh in the name of the Lord.

djk_text: Da wan kina dei, ne wan fu den edeman fu den Faliseiman kai Masaa Jesesi, fu a go nyan ne en osu. Ne Masaa Jesesi go. Ma namo, di a go, da ala sama ain be de ne en tapu.
eng_text: And it came to pass, as he went into the house of one of the chief Pharisees to eat bread on the sabbath day, that they watched him.

djk_text: Da wan man be de a ini a keliki di en hii sikin be soopu.
eng_text: And, behold, there was a certain man before him which had the dropsy.

djk_text: Ne Masaa Jesesi akisi den Faliseiman de anga den leliman fu Dyuweiti taki: “San u pakisei? A bun fu u deesi wan sama a kina dei, efu u mu fika en? San a weiti fu Mosesi taki fu dati?”
eng_text: And Jesus answering spake unto the lawyers and Pharisees, saying, Is it lawful to heal on the sabbath day?

djk_text: Ma ná wan fu den di piki en. Ne Masaa Jesesi langa ana oli a man, ne a deesi en te a kaba, ne a sende gwe.
eng_text: And they held their peace. And he took him, and healed him, and let him go;

djk_text: Ne a daai, ne a akisi den baka taki: “Efu wan fu u abi wan manpikin, ne a kai go a liba, da u o fika en fu a dede, fu di na kina dei ede, efu yu o lon go puu en? Soseefi, efu wan kaw fu u kai a liba, u o fika en fu a dede, fu di na kina dei ede?”
eng_text: And answered them, saying, Which of you shall have an ass or an ox fallen into a pit, and will not straightway pull him out on the sabbath day?

djk_text: Ma ná wan fu den di sabi fa fu piki en.
eng_text: And they could not answer him again to these things.

djk_text: Ne Masaa Jesesi luku ala den sama di kon na a fesa lontu te a kaba. Ne a si taki, sama de ape di wani sidon a wan moo hei peesi na a tafaa moo taawan. Bika den e hei denseefi. Ne a teke wan toli gi den.
eng_text: And he put forth a parable to those which were bidden, when he marked how they chose out the chief rooms; saying unto them,

djk_text: A taki: “Den sama, oo! Te wan sama kai u fu go ne en osu a wan piisii, da te u go, da u á mu suku fu go sidon na a moo hei peesi. Bika a sa de so taki, a sama di kai yu kon na a piisii de, kai taa sama tu, di hei moo yu.
eng_text: When thou art bidden of any man to a wedding, sit not down in the highest room; lest a more honourable man than thou be bidden of him;

djk_text: Da a o kon, da a taigi i, fi i opo go sidon, a baka, meke a taawan opo go sidon a fesi. Da anga gaan sen fanyaa, yu o opo go sidon na a moo lagi peesi a baka anda.
eng_text: And he that bade thee and him come and say to thee, Give this man place; and thou begin with shame to take the lowest room.

djk_text: “Te wan sama kai yu a wan fesa, da te i go, da sidon na a moo lagi peesi. Da te a sama si taki, pe i sidon de á fiti yu, da a sa kai yu taki: ‘Mi mati! Ná sidon faawe so. Kon sidon a mi dise.’ Da, te yu o opo, fu go sidon na a hei peesi de, da ala sama o si taki, i na wan hei sama tuu.
eng_text: But when thou art bidden, go and sit down in the lowest room; that when he that bade thee cometh, he may say unto thee, Friend, go up higher: then shalt thou have worship in the presence of them that sit at meat with thee.

djk_text: Bika a sama di e opo enseefi, sa booko saka. Ma a sama di saka enseefi den sa opo en.”
eng_text: For whosoever exalteth himself shall be abased; and he that humbleth himself shall be exalted.

djk_text: Ne Masaa Jesesi taigi a sama, di be kai en kon nyan ne en osu taki: “Te yu o kai sama fu kon nyan a yu osu moo, yu á mu kai den bun mati fi yu anga den baala fi i anga den famii fi i, efuso den guduman di e tan lontu yu wawan. Bika den sama ya sa du yu bun baka.
eng_text: Then said he also to him that bade him, When thou makest a dinner or a supper, call not thy friends, nor thy brethren, neither thy kinsmen, nor thy rich neighbours; lest they also bid thee again, and a recompence be made thee.

djk_text: Ma pe fu dati, da kai den pootiman anga den malengiiman anga den beendi ain wan anga den lanman meke den kon nyan anga yu.
eng_text: But when thou makest a feast, call the poor, the maimed, the lame, the blind:

djk_text: Da yu o fende seigi fi en. Bika den sowtu sama ya ná abi ná wan sani fu pai yu baka. Ma a dei, te Masaa Gadu o weki den sama di be libi bun ne en ain puu a dede, da a sa pai yu baka.”
eng_text: And thou shalt be blessed; for they cannot recompense thee: for thou shalt be recompensed at the resurrection of the just.

djk_text: Da di Masaa Jesesi taki so, ne wan fu den man di be sidon anga en a tafaa taki: “Da a musu de wan seigi fu sidon anga Masaa Gadu a tafaa, a ini a Nyun Tii fi en a Masaa Gadu Kondee a tapu anda.”
eng_text: And when one of them that sat at meat with him heard these things, he said unto him, Blessed is he that shall eat bread in the kingdom of God.

djk_text: Ne Masaa Jesesi piki en anga wan ageisi toli taki: “Wan sama oli wan gaan piisii wan dei. Ne a kai tyaipi sama kon na a piisii ya.
eng_text: Then said he unto him, A certain man made a great supper, and bade many:

djk_text: Ne di a seeka te a kaba, ne a sende wan wookoman fi en go kai den sama taki, meke den kon. Bika a yuu doo.
eng_text: And sent his servant at supper time to say to them that were bidden, Come; for all things are now ready.

djk_text: Ne a wookoman go, ne a kai den. Ne ala den fiya fende somen somen sani e taki, saide meke den ná o poi go. Wan fu den taki: ‘Man! Mi bai wan pisi doti, da mi mu go luku en. Taigi i basi gi mi taki, mi ná o poi kon, ye!’
eng_text: And they all with one consent began to make excuse. The first said unto him, I have bought a piece of ground, and I must needs go and see it: I pray thee have me excused.

djk_text: Wan taawan taigi en taki: ‘Taigi i basi taki, mi ná o poi kon. Bika mi bai tin kaw, da mi mu go wooko anga den luku.’
eng_text: And another said, I have bought five yoke of oxen, and I go to prove them: I pray thee have me excused.

djk_text: Wan taawan baka taigi en taki: ‘Man, a dyonson ya mi libi anga uman. Da taigi i basi gi mi taki, mi ná o poi kon, ye!’
eng_text: And another said, I have married a wife, and therefore I cannot come.

djk_text: “Ne a wookoman daai go gi en masaa den bosikopu. Ne a basi ati boon te, a ná sipowtu. Ne a sende a wookoman fi en baka taki: ‘Go esi esi, na ala den bakabini peesi fu a foto, da kai ala den pootiman anga malengiiman anga den lanman anga den beendiman fu den kon nyan anga mi.’
eng_text: So that servant came, and shewed his lord these things. Then the master of the house being angry said to his servant, Go out quickly into the streets and lanes of the city, and bring in hither the poor, and the maimed, and the halt, and the blind.

djk_text: Ne a wookoman go te a kon, ne a taigi a basi taki: ‘Basi den sama kon kaba, ma san mi si, da peesi fika ete.’
eng_text: And the servant said, Lord, it is done as thou hast commanded, and yet there is room.

djk_text: Ne a masaa piki en taki: ‘A bun! Go baka a den gaan paandasi anga den pikin kondee, da du moiti fu fende sama tyai kon moo. Bika a osu fu mi mu fuu.’
eng_text: And the lord said unto the servant, Go out into the highways and hedges, and compel them to come in, that my house may be filled.

djk_text: Mi e taigi u taki: ‘Ná wan fu den fosi sama di mi be kai, mofu sa tesi a nyanyan fu mi ya.’ ”
eng_text: For I say unto you, That none of those men which were bidden shall taste of my supper.

djk_text: Ma namo, da wan dei, Masaa Jesesi be e go a wan peesi. Da somen sama be kon ne en. Ne den waka, te wan pisi, ne a daai luku den.
eng_text: And there went great multitudes with him: and he turned, and said unto them,

djk_text: Ne a taigi den taki: “Efu wan sama wani de wan bakaman fu mi, da a mu lobi mi moo en mma anga en dda, anga en pikin anga den baala anga sisa fi en. Soseefi a mu lobi mi moo en eigi libi seefi. Efu a á du dati, da a ná o poi de wan bakaman fu mi.
eng_text: If any man come to me, and hate not his father, and mother, and wife, and children, and brethren, and sisters, yea, and his own life also, he cannot be my disciple.

djk_text: Efu wan sama wani toon bakaman fu mi, da a á mu teli enseefi moo. Da a mu de kaba kaba fu tyai den pina anga sitaafu di o kon ne en tapu fu mi ede. Awinsi a o dede seefi, toku a mu oli doo. A á mu daai baka.
eng_text: And whosoever doth not bear his cross, and come after me, cannot be my disciple.

djk_text: “Bika on di fu u de ya di e go sete wan osu, sondee fu a sidon pakisei bun fosi luku onmen moni a osu o teke? A mu sabi fosi efu a abi moni sai fu pai fu ala den sani.
eng_text: For which of you, intending to build a tower, sitteth not down first, and counteth the cost, whether he have sufficient to finish it?

djk_text: Efu a á du dati, da na den ponsu wawan a o beli, da a kaba. Da a á poi go moo faawe. Da den sama o lafu en, te a lafu. Da den o taki: ‘Luku de, a man de sete a osu, ma a fika afupasi, bika a ná abi moni sai.’
eng_text: Lest haply, after he hath laid the foundation, and is not able to finish it, all that behold it begin to mock him,

djk_text: “Da soseefi, efu wan kownu di abi tin dunsu suudati, wani go feti anga wan taa kownu di abi twenti dunsu suudati, da a o sidon pakisei bun fosi efu a sa feti anga en.
eng_text: Or what king, going to make war against another king, sitteth not down first, and consulteth whether he be able with ten thousand to meet him that cometh against him with twenty thousand?

djk_text: Ma, te a sidon pakisei te a kaba, ne a si taki a á poi feti anga a kownu fu den twenti dunsu suudati, da a o puu man sende go a fesi go begi a taa kownu meke den koo a toobi fosi den bigin feti.
eng_text: Or else, while the other is yet a great way off, he sendeth an ambassage, and desireth conditions of peace.

djk_text: Da na soseefi ibii wan fu u mu sidon pakisei bun fosi efu u sa fika ala den sani di u abi fu kon waka a mi baka. Da efu u á poi fika den, da u ná o poi toon bakaman fu mi.
eng_text: So likewise, whosoever he be of you that forsaketh not all that he hath, he cannot be my disciple.

djk_text: “We, bika u luku. Sawtu na wan bun sani. Ma efu a lasi en kaakiti, da san a bun fu du moo? Na fu teke, da u towe a dyiko.
eng_text: Salt is good: but if the salt have lost his savour, wherewith shall it be seasoned?

djk_text: Da fa i si yu o towe en a dyiko de seefi, da a ná a doti fu a dyiko seefi a o poi fatu, fu goo sani. A ná abi ná wankodo yeepi moo. Da fa mi taki anga u ya, u pakisei bun fu u sa fusutan en bunbun.”
eng_text: It is neither fit for the land, nor yet for the dunghill; but men cast it out. He that hath ears to hear, let him hear.

djk_text: Ma namo, wan dei, ne den sama di e piki lantimoni anga den sama di be abi polinen a kondee go aliki Masaa Jesesi.
eng_text: Then drew near unto him all the publicans and sinners for to hear him.

djk_text: Ne den Faliseiman anga den leliman fu Dyuweiti si Masaa Jesesi e hulu anga den takuu libi sowtu sama de. Ne den teke Masaa Jesesi fu ogii. Den taki: “A man ya na wan bunbun sama tan so? Ne fa a waka ai hulu den takuu libi sowtu sama de? Son toon seefi a nái sen fu nyan anga den. Da na wan bunbun sama tan so?”
eng_text: And the Pharisees and scribes murmured, saying, This man receiveth sinners, and eateth with them.

djk_text: Ne di Masaa Jesesi sabi taki, na so den e kuutu en, ne a gi den wan ageisi toli fu soi den saide meke ai du dati. A taki:
eng_text: And he spake this parable unto them, saying,

djk_text: “U aliki mi bun! Meke u taki wan fu u abi wan ondoo sikapu. Ne i tyai den go poti a sabana fu den nyan. Ne wan fu den komoto a den taawan mindii go lasi, san yu o du? Yu ná o seeka den taa neigintenti a neigin te a kaba, da i go suku awan kodo di lasi fu te i fende en, no?
eng_text: What man of you, having an hundred sheep, if he lose one of them, doth not leave the ninety and nine in the wilderness, and go after that which is lost, until he find it?

djk_text: Da, te i fende en kaba, da yu o diki en poti a sikoo anga gaan piisii, da i go a kondee. Da yu o kai den mati fi yu anga den sama di e tan lontu yu, da i taigi den taki: ‘U meke piisii anga mi! Bika wan sikapu fu mi be lasi, ma mi fende en baka.’
eng_text: And when he hath found it, he layeth it on his shoulders, rejoicing.

djk_text: We, fa i si ala sama e piisii anga yu de, na soseefi piisii de a Masaa Gadu tu, te wan takuulibi sama daai libi. Da den e piisii anga en, moo enke den neigintenti a neigin, di ná abi fu daai libi moo.”
eng_text: I say unto you, that likewise joy shall be in heaven over one sinner that repenteth, more than over ninety and nine just persons, which need no repentance.

djk_text: Ne Masaa Jesesi taigi den baka taki: “We soseefi, efu wan uman abi tin solufu moni, ne wan kai lasi a ini en osu. Na leti a o leti faya e sibi a hii osu, e suku fu te a fende en baka, no?
eng_text: Either what woman having ten pieces of silver, if she lose one piece, doth not light a candle, and sweep the house, and seek diligently till she find it?

djk_text: Da, te a fende en, da a o kai den mati fi en anga ala den sama di e tan lontu en, da a taigi den taki: ‘U meke piisii anga mi. Bika wan solufu moni fu mi be lasi, ma mi fende en baka.’
eng_text: And when she hath found it, she calleth her friends and her neighbours together, saying, Rejoice with me; for I have found the piece which I had lost.

djk_text: We, fa i si den sama e piisii fu di den fende awan kodo solufu moni di be lasi de, da na soseefi den Basiya fu Masaa Gadu Kondee seefi e piisii tu, te wan kodo takuulibi sama daai en libi.”
eng_text: Likewise, I say unto you, there is joy in the presence of the angels of God over one sinner that repenteth.

djk_text: Ne Masaa Jesesi taigi den baka taki: “Wan man be de. Da a be abi tu manpikin.
eng_text: And he said, A certain man had two sons:

djk_text: Di den de, te wan dei, ne a moo pikinwan kon ne en taki: ‘Mi dda! Mi wani i paati a gudu, da i gi mi fu mi se di mi be o fende wanten. Ne a dda paati a gudu, ne a gi den manpikin fu den se.’
eng_text: And the younger of them said to his father, Father, give me the portion of goods that falleth to me. And he divided unto them his living.

djk_text: “Da wantu dei a baka, ne a moo pikinwan teke ala en gudu, ne a go a wan faawe kondee. Da na a pe a poli ala a moni fi en anga yayo libi.
eng_text: And not many days after the younger son gathered all together, and took his journey into a far country, and there wasted his substance with riotous living.

djk_text: Ne di a de te wan pisi, ne wan gaan angiiten kon na a kondee. Ne ai pina tee, na fu dede namo. Bika a á be abi ná wan enkii moni moo. A be poli ala fosi a gaan angiiten ya doo.
eng_text: And when he had spent all, there arose a mighty famine in that land; and he began to be in want.

djk_text: Ne a go suku wooko a wan sama fu a kondee. Ne a sama teke en a wooko fu ai luku den agu fi en gi en.
eng_text: And he went and joined himself to a citizen of that country; and he sent him into his fields to feed swine.

djk_text: Angii kii en te, a be wani den nyanyan fu den agu fu nyan. Ma dati seefi den á wani gi en.
eng_text: And he would fain have filled his belly with the husks that the swine did eat: and no man gave unto him.

djk_text: “Ne a de ape, te wan pisi, ne a kisi enseefi. Ne a taki: ‘San! Na mi kon tan so? Mi, di mi dda abi onmen tenti wookoman e gi nyanyan den e nyan, te den bee fuu. Ne na mi kon tan ya e pina a pina ya?
eng_text: And when he came to himself, he said, How many hired servants of my father's have bread enough and to spare, and I perish with hunger!

djk_text: I sabi san? Mi o daai go baka a mi dda. Da mi o taigi en taki: “Mi dda. Mi du ogii anga yu anga Masaa Gadu seefi.
eng_text: I will arise and go to my father, and will say unto him, Father, I have sinned against heaven, and before thee,

djk_text: Da mi á waiti moo seefi fi i oli mi enke wan manpikin fi yu. Ma gaantangi baa, teke mi enke wan wookoman fi yu namo a wooko.” ’
eng_text: And am no more worthy to be called thy son: make me as one of thy hired servants.

djk_text: “Ne a opo, ne a daai go ne en dda baka. Ne a waka te a opo uku. A di en dda luku, ne a si wan sama, te a faawe anda e kon. Ne tyali fu a pikin kisi en. Ne a dyombo peb, lon go miti en a pasi. Ne a kisi en gwulu baasa, bosi, piisii anga en, te a bigi.
eng_text: And he arose, and came to his father. But when he was yet a great way off, his father saw him, and had compassion, and ran, and fell on his neck, and kissed him.

djk_text: Ne a pikin taki: ‘Mi dda! Mi á waiti sai fu yu oli mi enke yu manpikin moo. Bika, mi du ogii anga yu anga Masaa Gadu seefi. Ma gaantangi! Teke mi a wooko enke wan wookoman fi yu namo, baa?’
eng_text: And the son said unto him, Father, I have sinned against heaven, and in thy sight, and am no more worthy to be called thy son.

djk_text: “Ma, fosi a kaba taki, ne a dda bali gi den wookoman taki: ‘U esi go teke den moo waiti koosi kon wei gi en. U tyai wan linga kon wei ne en finga gi en. U tyai susu kon gi en meke a wei ne en futu.
eng_text: But the father said to his servants, Bring forth the best robe, and put it on him; and put a ring on his hand, and shoes on his feet:

djk_text: Da u go kii a moo fatu kaw tyai kon, meke u boli nyan meke piisii anga a manpikin fu mi ya.
eng_text: And bring hither the fatted calf, and kill it; and let us eat, and be merry:

djk_text: Bika a manpikin fu mi ya, be lasi fu go kaba a soso, ma a daai kon baka.’ Ne den meke gaan piisii anga en.
eng_text: For this my son was dead, and is alive again; he was lost, and is found. And they began to be merry.

djk_text: “Da a ten de, da a gaan baala be de a ini goon e wooko. Ne di a komoto a goon e kon, ne a yee den e pee, e meke piisii e dansi.
eng_text: Now his elder son was in the field: and as he came and drew nigh to the house, he heard musick and dancing.

djk_text: Ne a kai wan fu den wookoman fi en dda, ne a akisi en taki: ‘San pasa ya?’
eng_text: And he called one of the servants, and asked what these things meant.

djk_text: Ne a piki en taki: ‘We, na a pikin baala fi yu di i si be gwe, ne en daai kon baka a osu. Ne i si a dda kii a fatu kaw e meke piisii anga en, fu di a daai kon gusontu gusontu libilibi a osu baka.’
eng_text: And he said unto him, Thy brother is come; and thy father hath killed the fatted calf, because he hath received him safe and sound.

djk_text: “Ne di a gaan baala yee so, ne en ati boon te, a á wani go a ini osu. Ne di en dda yee so, ne a go ne en. Ne a taigi en taki: ‘Biya, kon a osu!’
eng_text: And he was angry, and would not go in: therefore came his father out, and intreated him.

djk_text: Ne a taki: ‘Nono! Mi ná o kon a osu. Bika luku on langa mi anga yu de ya. Ná wan dei di mi pasa i mofu, gaanengee gi yu. Ala san i sende mi, mi e du enke fa i sende mi. Mi e wooko e naki mi sikin gi yu enke sitaafuman. Ma ná wan pikin kaabita seefi di i gi mi, fu mi kii nyan meke piisii anga den mati fu mi.
eng_text: And he answering said to his father, Lo, these many years do I serve thee, neither transgressed I at any time thy commandment: and yet thou never gavest me a kid, that I might make merry with my friends:

djk_text: Ma di a manpikin fi yu di teke i gudu go poli anga wisiwasi yayo libi daai kon baka, ne i kii a fatu kaw, meke sowan gaan piisii gi en.’
